The hunt for World of Warcraft: Forever secrets continue with the discovery of an elusive pet

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (350 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the search for secrets in World of Warcraft: Forever continues ever onwards, with a latest breakthrough coming to light in recent days.
  • The cat's name is Ta'Shkal, and they can be found on Mount Hyjal.
  • Recent findings suggest that the way you do so is relatively simple.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the search for secrets in World of Warcraft: Forever continues ever onwards, with a latest breakthrough coming to light in recent days. The latest discovery? An elusive new cat that can be tamed by hunters in one of the game's new zones.

The cat's name is Ta'Shkal, and they can be found on Mount Hyjal. An endgame levelling zone, players will have to reach at least level 57 in order to safely make their way up there and recruit this upcoming pet.

Recent findings suggest that the way you do so is relatively simple. You need to find a small corrupted cat figuring within the Felblood Scar region of Mount Hyjal. Once you've found that, you then need to travel up to a hidden lantern south of the Mourning's Rest area. With the figurine in your bags, you'll be able to interact with the lantern, spawning the cat for you to tame (granted you're playing a hunter).

Recent findings suggest that so what's the significant deal about this cat? Well, aside from the fact it's got a strange colour scheme of green fur with orange stripes, the cat also has a base attack speed of 1.0. This means it'll attack once every second, which is pretty fast and allows for greater damage output from your pet. This inherently makes the pet valuable for endgame hunter players, who are looking to improve their performance in PvE and PvP.

It has been revealed that this is not the only secret discovered by World of Warcraft: Forever sleuths. Last week, they pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. As of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

According to recent reports, the game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among new and returning players. It's the biggest launch in the series' history, and has gone down well with people so far. Even if it has recently suffered its first controversy with a now-fixed gold exploit.

Sex in GTA 6 was extremely difficult to pull off, Rockstar claims

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Implementing sex into GTA 6 in a believable way was quite tricky to pull off, according to developer Rockstar Games.
  • In a recent development, this being both a Grand Theft Auto game and a love story, it's not a shocker that sex and intimacy (and the most nudity I've ever seen in a video game) are so prominent in GTA 6.
  • "Exploring the physical relationship between Jason and Lucia required a lot of thought and iteration," Rockstar's vice president of animation, Mark Tennant, explains in quotes given to GamesRadar ahead of our GTA 6 review.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Implementing sex into GTA 6 in a believable way was quite tricky to pull off, according to developer Rockstar Games.

In a recent development, this being both a Grand Theft Auto game and a love story, it's not a shocker that sex and intimacy (and the most nudity I've ever seen in a video game) are so prominent in GTA 6. Getting the balance just right was pretty tough, however.

"Exploring the physical relationship between Jason and Lucia required a lot of thought and iteration," Rockstar's vice president of animation, Mark Tennant, explains in quotes given to GamesRadar ahead of our GTA 6 review.

"We needed to allow players to interact with the partner in a natural, loving way, with a believable progression based on their overall investment in the relationship," he adds. GTA 6's romance isn't a totally linear line. Jason and Lucia can be hotly passionate about each other or just be cordial partners in crime, depending on your choices, so how they interact physically needed to match their relationship status.

"This required us to create animation performances that found a realistic balance between player agency and partner response while keeping things fun, passionate, and rewarding," Tennant says.

According to recent reports, it's a far cry from how many of the other games in the series dealt with sex, where your main interactions with romantic partners were impersonal and often transactional. On the flip side, GTA 6 is almost always making you consider someone outside of yourself and sex isn't just an awkward animation that plays if you drop some in-game cash. Jason and Lucia's central romance is the reason why Rockstar isn't letting you hire prostitutes this time around, too.

Walmart’s early Black Friday sale just kicked off, offering no shortage of worthy tech deals, and one home audio deal in particular has our attention. If you’re looking to level up your home theater audio setup for less, the Vizio 4.1 Pro SV410YW-10 Soundbar and wireless surround speakers setup with Dolby Atmos and DTS:X support is on sale for $79 (originally $148), a nearly 50% discount.

The two pre-paired wireless surround speakers can be positioned behind or beside your seating area, while two bass drivers built into the 32-inch soundbar mean you don’t need a separate subwoofer. The system maxes out at 95 dB, with bass extending to 50 Hz.

It has been revealed that the SV410YW-1 connects to your television through HDMI eARC and supports CEC, so you can adjust the volume with your TV remote. While its integrated subwoofers won’t give you the same impressive low end as a dedicated unit, this system still delivers robust, bassy sound that goes far beyond built-in TV speakers. There’s an added perk for Vizio TV owners—it can be attached directly beneath the screen using the QuickFit feature.

According to recent reports, along with the deal are additional promos, like up to two free months of Apple Music and up to a free month of Apple TV. If your current TV sound setup is lacking some oomph and you want an under-$100 upgrade with a subwoofer and soundbar, the Vizio 4.1 Pro SV410YW-10 Soundbar and wireless surround speaker combo is a good choice for the money.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that panache Digital Games will release the first major content update for the Early Access version of dark third-person narrative action adventure game 1666: Amsterdam in December, the developer announced. It will expand the game’s world, story, and supernatural abilities.

The December enhancement marks the first major expansion of the Early Access experience, bringing newly introduced areas to explore, new supernatural abilities, and another Original for players to confront.

A New Region, a New Original, and More Witchcraft.

Arriving during the final moon of the year, the first major enhancement marks the beginning of a series of planned expansions for 1666: Amsterdam.

In a recent development, players will be able to explore Ouderkerk, a new region slightly larger than the game’s right now available area, effectively doubling the world players can explore. Alongside this new location comes another Esbat and a new Original, bringing the next chapter of Noa’s journey to Early Access.

The update will also introduce additional Lux and Nux spells and combos, along with new jewels and potions, giving players more ways to develop their abilities and approach encounters.

Panache Digital Games will share more details about these additions in the weeks leading up to the December release.

■ Early Access Price Remains Unchanged.

Panache Digital Games has also confirmed that 1666: Amsterdam will remain at its current Early Access price when the December patch debuts, with no price increase for the upcoming content.

This first major update is part of the team’s ongoing Early Access roadmap, with further expansions planned as development continues.

1666: Amsterdam is available now in Early Access for PC via Steam and Epic Games Store.

Darkest Dungeon 2's next bit of DLC is a short run, combat focused gauntlet where you must do everything in your power to please the audience

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (358 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the original Darkest Dungeon may have gotten some new DLC earlier this year, but that doesn't mean that Red Hook Studios are abandoning their sequel.
  • It's called The Butcher's Asylum, as pleasant a name as any other, and it's a "stand alone gladiatorial arena game mode," that's due for release sometime in 2027.
  • This DLC isn't veering too far away from its roguelite origins, as it is still run-based, just on the shorter side and focusing more on the combat system.

It has been revealed that the original Darkest Dungeon may have gotten some new DLC earlier this year, but that doesn't mean that Red Hook Studios are abandoning their sequel. No, in fact the next bit of DLC for Darkest Dungeon 2 was teased only a couple of weeks ago, with a new trailer shared today actually showing off what it's all about.

It's called The Butcher's Asylum, as pleasant a name as any other, and it's a "stand alone gladiatorial arena game mode," that's due for release sometime in 2027. "The long-silent bells of the remote Asylum ring once more - souring the valley below with discordant and unsettling vibrations," the DLC's Steam page describes. "Garish heraldry, hastily stitched by unskilled hands, festoons the hilltop. Deep within the crumbling masonry of the Asylum, frenzied inmates compete in merciless bloodsport with monsters corralled the kingdom over. And to the victors of these debauched contests, the Butcher’s favour: a cure for their madness.".

This DLC isn't veering too far away from its roguelite origins, as it is still run-based, just on the shorter side and focusing more on the combat system. On your runs you'll need to prepare for the fights ahead, come across "insane enemy combinations never before possible," and spin a fun wheel which nets you prizes like newly introduced battle modifiers, charms and jinxes. There's also a new crowd meter, "a unique feature to the Asylum, can grant powerful effects to your team if you cater to the Crowd's demands. Failing to do so will only earn their scorn which raises the stakes and puts your success in jeopardy!".

Recent findings suggest that the Butcher's Asylum also introduces a new playable character, The Ringmaster. You pick her up by winning bouts in the arena, and then you can recruit her in any game mode. She also serves as the narrator for the DLC, likely because of the passing of the main game's narrator Wayne June; Red Hook made clear earlier this year that they would never use generative AI to recreate June's voice, so I'm glad to see they haven't backstracked here.

Ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs. Per the CEO, the industry's move away from physical games and towards a digital-only future is harmful to both consumers and businesses.

In an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend. Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop.".

These comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch. The game, expected to be the biggest video game launch of all time, is not shipping on discs at all. Even if you purchase a physical copy of the game, what you will actually take home is a 'code in a box' - giving you a code you can redeem on your console of choice that entitles you to a digital version of the game. GTA 6 is not the first game to do this, but it is the most high-profile. Similarly to discs, codes are also region-locked (at least on the PS5), meaning that the proliferation of codes as a format isn't even helping make games more readily available in certain markets.

According to recent reports, cohen notes he's been in conversation with "the obvious [publishers]" but that he's had little sway on their prepares. "Of course they don’t like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying new," he told Bloomberg. "They're taking away competition.".

Sources indicate that though Cohen doesn't name GTA 6 specifically in the Bloomberg interview, it's clear that he's talking about Rockstar's megaton launch (he explicitly tweeted "GTA. On a disc. In a case. On your shelf. Like if you still want a physical copy" two days ago). The lack of trade-in potential is clearly harming his business; the Bloomberg article reveals pre-owned and refurbished products make up 22% of the GameStop's sales, down 32 percent from the same time a year ago.

Recent findings suggest that of course, the proliferation of game-in-a-box products doesn't end with GTA 6. Sony plans to stop producing physical discs for latest PlayStation games starting in January 2028, moving to a digital-only model despite pushback from consumers and certain developers and publishers. The outcry is doing little to influence Sony's decision, however.

Disc or no disc, GTA 6 is expected to cross $2bn in its opening weekend, and at the moment that is looking like a conservative figure, too. It's estimated the game has sold well over 19.05m units at the time of writing. Despite the astronomical sales, though, employees at Rockstar are still worried about layoffs. Additionally, a tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members (who were fired for apparent breaches of their NDAs) just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Bethesda got its hands on the Fallout licence way back in 2004, the naysayers were many and vocal.

  • For clarity's sake, the angry fans at the time were likely Black Isle and Interplay fans rather than Obsidian fans—the latter studio hadn't ever made a Fallout game in 2004 (though it had Fallout alumni on staff), and they were prophesying (after 2006) that Bethesda's take on Fallout would be like Oblivion, not Skyrim, since the latter released in 2011.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Bethesda got its hands on the Fallout licence way back in 2004, the naysayers were many and vocal. In fairness, the naysayers are still many and vocal, but they were back then too, and it turns out Bethesda saw at least a few of their posts. In a chat with The Examined Game, Skyrim lead Bruce Nesmith reflected on the reaction some Fallout old-heads had to Bethesda's acquisition of the series.

"There was huge pushback when Bethesda got the Fallout licence to do Fallout 3. There was a lot of people who were Obsidian fans, who were like 'Bethesda's gonna screw it up, they're just gonna make it Skyrim, we want Fallout the way we remember Fallout', and there was a strong, vocal community that just hated that we were gonna make that game".

For clarity's sake, the angry fans at the time were likely Black Isle and Interplay fans rather than Obsidian fans—the latter studio hadn't ever made a Fallout game in 2004 (though it had Fallout alumni on staff), and they were prophesying (after 2006) that Bethesda's take on Fallout would be like Oblivion, not Skyrim, since the latter released in 2011. I suspect Nesmith is muddling the initial negative reaction with, well, the more modern one, which is shaped in large part by Obsidian's excellent Fallout: Latest Vegas from 2010.

Recent findings suggest that "We had to prove them wrong", recalls Nesmith, "and fortunately we did, because Fallout 3 was embraced even by a lot of our sceptics". It's true: people bloody loved Fallout 3 and still do, though there are of course still series fans who reject the game. "There's always going to be some diehard people that say 'Fallout 2 was the greatest Fallout game ever', but we tried our best to just not engage… because you're not going to win that argument.

"All you can do is make the best game you can and let that be your statement. And that's what Bethesda did".

Does the vitriol ever get to Bethesda and its devs? Unsurprisingly, yeah, a little. "Any time somebody says that the thing you're doing is, you know, fill in your blank for all the cuss words and the bad things… you feel like it's a statement about yourself. You have to divorce yourself from that [but] you can't help but take it a little bit personally. But it does make you want to prove them wrong. It does make you want to say 'I'm going to show you that this will work, that we can respect the franchise and make it better and make it our way, rather than the old way".

  • But in typical tricky Tony fashion, there's an update for chapter seven where he makes it sound like no one but him knows how the whole game is going to end.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toby Fox is a purposefully mysterious person. It was probably a wise choice on his part, obfuscating his current appearance with everyone's favourite annoying dog, essentially never speaking aloud in livestreams and instead using a text-to-speech bot, and posting only when there's notable enough Deltarune updates of if it would be very funny. But as it turns out, that sense of mystery extends to the team that's making Deltarune too, as Fox won't tell his devs how the game ends until they've built enough of it.

Sources indicate that earlier this week, the fall edition of the Deltarune newsletter went out, offering a brief revision on the game's next and sixth chapter. That one's apparently now a "structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end," but that doesn't mean it's quite ready for release, as "some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation." I'd expect a 2027 release for this chapter, which is going to be a shorter one too.

But in typical tricky Tony fashion, there's an update for chapter seven where he makes it sound like no one but him knows how the whole game is going to end. "Well, we've only just started…," he explains of the progress. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way.".

Sources indicate that I'm glad they all think it's fun, the wait for me personally certainly ain't. I do wonder if this speaks to a certain anxiety over how the game will shape up. Following the release of chapter five I was subjected to all manner of theories about what's to come by my partner gorging on YouTube videos from folks who mostly just seem quite excited about it all, even if a lot of them sound wrong. So I imagine there must be a little bit of weight to all of those varying expectations.

Recent findings suggest that fox did note in the newsletter that "unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence...!" so perhaps I'm speaking a load of hogwash! That said, I'm furious that a character called Apple Girlington didn't make it into chapter five, so you can expect to hear from my lawyers, Mr. Fox.

GTA 6 has replaced websites with social media and phone apps because "it didn't feel necessary"

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.
  • Recent findings suggest that the web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps.
  • It has been revealed that "It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.

Recent findings suggest that the web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps. The reason? Smartphone apps just made more sense.

It has been revealed that "It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku. "We definitely wanted to lean into apps and create these apps.".

According to recent reports, though some of the apps in GTA 6 perform similar tasks to the web of old, Nelson remarked the team didn't want players to be distracted from the game's detailed open world by staring at screens. That also extends to getting players to appreciate the value of money, and witnessing the progression of Jason and Lucia as they go from pawnshop robberies to staging major bank heists.

"They don't really need websites to be buying a lot of shit, you know what I mean, and so everything grows very organically," Nelson said, adding that websites may return in the future.

"I remember asking Stu Petri, our head of 2D and UI, about websites, and he was like, 'For what? What do you need it for?' So, that was it," he added.

In materials supplied by Rockstar ahead of our review, Sam Grosset (associate UI director at the studio) also explained that a lot of thought went into how the apps work, and how easily the phone needed to fit into your play style in order for it to work as effectively as possible.

In a recent development, "We ensure the UI feels like a natural extension of the game world, supporting players without interrupting gameplay or breaking immersion, unless necessary to do so," stated Grosset. "The UI should be complementary to the game and appropriate for each scenario. It was a big shift for our phone interface to be in-hand, but it supports that feeling of playing as Jason or Lucia and helps us stay embedded in the world.".

Rockstar would continually "raise the bar, question assumptions, explore newly introduced possibilities, and learn through rigorous testing and iteration" in order to make these apps - and the UX/UI in general - feel in line with the production quality of the rest of the game.

In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, Chris Tapsell awarded the open-world crime game five stars, raving about its absurd level of detail, compelling characters, exciting action and of its substantial heart.

If you're looking to spend the next several days playing Rockstar's latest hit, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough has detailed guides on everything from individual missions, to core mechanics like the fresh Wanted Level, and relationship and romance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that getting a tank in GTA 6 represents the pinnacle of criminal behavior, and there's a long history of stealing Rhinos going all the way back through the series to GTA 3! These military vehicles are virtually indestructible so you're safely protected inside, and they pack a powerful enough punch with their cannon to destroy anything GTA 6 puts in front of you. You also need to get inside one to unlock the Challenging Tank Trophy or Achievement, so to help you out with that, here's how to steal a tank in GTA 6.

Industry observers note that the location for an entire row of GTA 6 tanks is in the Mile Zero Air Station, situated west of the area you begin the story in, which you can reach by driving through Abismo Key and on to Southwind. You'll need a vehicle to break into the military base which will get left behind, so it's best not to use your GTA 6 personal vehicle for this job, and equipping body armor from Ammu-nation is highly recommended for added protection.

By following the route marked on my map above you'll weave through several road barriers, as which point the soldiers will open fire on you, then turn right at the first opportunity to pass more barriers and soldiers until you spot a handy pile of dirt. You must use this Stunt Jump to clear the perimeter fence, though if you don't get enough height to also clear the inner fence you can smash through it to reach the runway.

In a recent development, look to your left when on the miliary runway and you'll see a large building, and to the left of that are the Rhino tanks we're looking for – you can also head to the right of that building if you'd prefer to grab a GTA 6 jet instead. Once you reach the tanks, crash through the fence and then approach one before using the usual enter vehicle button to climb in through the front hatch. Note that there is various military hardware in this area, but the Rhino tanks are the ones closest to the fence you broke through.

You can then drive away in your newly introduced GTA 6 tank, which will shortly unlock the Challenging Tank award from the GTA 6 Trophy and Achievement list to add to your collection. Strangely, commandeering this military vehicle doesn't initially increase your GTA 6 Wanted Level beyond the existing two-stars for breaking into the base, though this soon goes to five and then six-stars when you start blasting things with your cannon.

Sources indicate that don't expect to get too far in your Rhino tank, as it drives pretty slowly and you're being constantly peppered with incoming gunfire plus rockets from helicopters – which you can shoot down if you aim your barrel high enough. However, the tank will eventually run out of fuel or become so damaged that it is completely incapacitated, and as surrender is no longer an option the upcoming Wasted is unavoidable.

The Wanted Level you get won't affect your current GTA 6 criminal profile, though you can only get a six-star Wanted level in GTA 6 if you go all in on a psychotic rampage!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, publisher GRYPHLINE and developer Mountain Contour will release the version revision “Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms” for free-to-play 3D RPG Arknights: Endfield on November 25, the companies announced. The game’s latest live stream also introduced the upcoming version 2.0 update, which takes players to Gypsosia and aboard the Rhodes Island landship, and teased 10 characters who will join the journey across upcoming content updates.

“With Wuling’s story wrapping up, and the main story taking us through all the heavy moments, we want to give you a change of pace with a lighthearted, upbeat patch,” mentioned Arknights: Endfield producer Light Zhong in a press release.

Here is an overview of the revision, via GRYPHLINE:.

Version Enhancement “Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms”.

Strange mushrooms have overrun an abandoned dam outside Wuling, where Landbreakers worship a giant mushroom and visitors keep slipping into hallucinations. There, the Endministrator meets Kay, a Rhodes Island Operator who has been adventuring alone across Talos-II in search of them. Kay happily shares everything she treasures, including a towering stack of honey waffles. But which would she choose: a mountain of waffles or a dear friend?

A Nature Vanguard with a carefree fighting style, Kay throws weapons that scatter across the battlefield, then gathers them up for a heavy hammer slam. Along the way, she drops Picnic Snacks that heal her teammates.

According to recent reports, the Old Dam, the enhancement’s upcoming area, has grown into a fairytale-like mushroom kingdom. Players fire Kay’s honey waffles at mushrooms to open doors and spin fungal bridges, and must avoid Loquacious Shrooms that scramble their sense of direction. Mushroom foes like the Bolete Prince guard the dam, and a mushroom as tall as a mountain waits at its heart.

In a recent development, the update’s music leans into its whimsical tone, with Ori composer Gareth Coker and ambient producer Owsey returning to score Kay’s honey waffle adventure. It caps a first year in which the soundtrack has followed the story, from the sweeping sci-fi orchestral sound of Valley IV to the choir-driven battle against Alleikhreos, Typhoeus’s JRPG-inspired winter journey and the modern electronic take on Eastern music in Si’s painted world.

Industry observers note that later in the update, every player who logs in during the Workers’ Guards: Roll Call event will receive the Operator Mimino and her signature weapon, Star of Tomorrow, for free, with event missions offering extra copies to reach full Potential. Operators Gilberta and Rossi also return in successive reruns.

For factory builders, Exclusion Zone Rebuilding is a new permanent mode in which players supply materials across four phases to restore the North Wuling Exclusion Zone, using the new Forge of Luminance to transform products on their conveyor belts. For a lighter break, Lucky Carrot’s Games of Wonder adds two multiplayer card games, Witch’s Darkjack and Band Uprising, that players can enjoy with friends or through matchmaking.

A First Look at Version 2.0 and Rhodes Island.

The livestream also previewed the next chapter of Arknights: Endfield, arriving in the new year. Exiles have launched attacks across the Civilization Band, and their real target is Rhodes Island. The Endministrator sets out with Perlica into Gypsosia, the Cretaceous Frontiers, where players will be able to board and explore Rhodes Island itself, a massive landship. A 10-character teaser offered a glimpse of companions for the journey, including Warfarin, appearing as the leader of Rhodes Island, and M3, who returns looking completely different.

Industry observers note that the chapter’s first update will add four latest maps at once, including Rhodes Island. Main Mission Early Unlock: Gypsosia will let players who have completed the main mission Remediation Progress skip ahead to the new story while still earning all beginner-event rewards. New modes are also in development for future updates, including a management sim with the Golden Branch Tribe and the Shattered Protocol combat mode.

Arknights: Endfield is now Steam Deck Verified, with default controller support and every feature available on Valve’s handheld. The update also brings Despot Weaponized, a newly introduced high-difficulty challenge series in Umbral Monument; the return of RISE! MEGA ARENA!, a two-Operator arena event; and new seasons of the Echoes of War combat mode.

Arknights: Endfield is available now for PlayStation 5, PC via the official launcher, Steam, and Epic Games Store, iOS via App Store, and Android via Google Play.

Oh I do love an eldritch horror creature, I do, especially one that at first glance may only be slightly different from what I'm used to seeing. Eldritch Empathy, then, seems like a grand ole game to satisfy my wanton need to experience such things. It's a puzzle roguelite that isn't exactly a Papers Please-like but certainly feels reminiscent of one, where you have to "analyse corrupted creatures, purify their emotions and learn how to communicate with an eldritch being.".

You kick things off by embodying Eike, a "young woman who has strange dreams and sightings of twisted creatures in the woodlands neighbouring the sleepy Swiss village she lives in." She decides to investigate these mysterious circumstances herself, where she comes upon these corrupted critters in the woods. You need to thoroughly inspect them, using a book to determine what is going on with them and what they need exactly; it's akin to checking the passport rulebook in Papers Please, hence the comparison.

After figuring out what's going on with these creatures, you then "use and transform symbols to create paths through the creatures' insides. You may use care and precision to navigate to the correct corrupted emotion you have identified from your investigation and purify it. You may also use your tools to cause harm. Whatever you choose, your actions will have consequences." Ominous! You can also plan your runs ahead of time, heading down paths that may offer you some boons here and there, like the option to restore a bit of sanity (it's one of those Lovecraftian kind of horror games, as loathe as I am that we still have to reference that guy).

Also be wary of the fact that actions you take out in the woods can affect your home and community. It's a roguelite with consequences! Mwahahha! Looks pretty neat overall, and has some tasty pixel art attached to it too. No release date just yet, but I'd assume it'll arrive no earlier than next year. You can wishlist it right here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite its somewhat muted critical reception, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has predictably topped the US video game charts in October. The Infinity Ward-developed shooter was October's best-selling game in the US across digital and retail, beating the month's other major-hitters, including Gears of War: E-Day and Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

That's according to market analysis firm Circana's latest US market report, which revealed Modern Warfare 4 was October's leader in dollar sales. This marks the 19th-year running that a Call of Duty game topped the charts in its release month, a streak that began with November 2008's COD: World at War.

However, despite a successful October, Modern Warfare 4 hasn't managed to land in Circana's top ten list of year-to-date biggest sellers. In fact, the only COD title on the list is the Black Ops 2 port released this summer. NBA 2K27 continues to lead Circana's ranking, having overtaken Resident Evil: Requiem last month to secure the top spot. It's a reverse of Circana's September report, when NBA 2K27 failed to lead its own debut month but claimed the top spot in the year-to-date list. Here's the list of the top 10 year-to-date:.

It has been revealed that away from Modern Warfare 4, October saw the release of several other well-performing and critically acclaimed games, and six of the top ten were new releases. That hasn't stopped Circana from posting 14 percent lower spending on games compared to October last year. Analyst Mat Piscatella noted much of that dip can be attributed to a significant slump in mobile spending, and also because October 2025 was particularly strong, with both Battlefield 6 and Pokémon Legends: Z-A releasing. Here's October's top 10:.

According to recent reports, in Eurogamer's Modern Warfare 4 review, Dom Peppiatt awarded it four stars, writing: "Modern Warfare 4 represents the highest tide for Call of Duty in seven years. Infinity Ward needed to pull off a balancing act I don't envy; injecting just enough nostalgia into a series propped up with so many conventions and expectations there's barely room for anything fresh, alongside enough innovation and intrigue to keep people interested.".

According to recent reports, deciding whether to proceed or postpone the Protective Custody story mission is a major choice you'll need to make in GTA 6. The mission appears on your map as "Meet Abe" in Chapter 5, once you've completed the mission Operation Savage Glory.

According to recent reports, once you get to Abe's office, Jason will warn Lucia that everything will change after this mission. Lucia will hesitate at the door as you make your choice to "Proceed" or "Postpone.".

Sources indicate that this is a pretty massive decision, because Protective Custody kicks off the final mission of the game which takes about an hour to play. And even though it's a binary choice between "Proceed" (which starts the mission) and "Postpone" (which delays the mission)" there's actually a third possible outcome based on when you make the choice.

It's a long mission that will take about an hour to play, so be prepared. You can't save during this mission so make sure you've got the time! Once you've completed the final mission, you can watch the credits and return to the open world so you can continue playing.

Industry observers note that you will go back to the open world to continue playing. The "Meet Abe" icon will remain on your map so you can begin the final mission at any point from then on.

There are multiple endings to GTA 6, and I won't spoil them here. But one of the endings is only possible if you postpone the Protective Custody mission until you've deposited $2 million into your Buck Me savings account. That's why when you choose to proceed with the final mission makes a difference.

According to recent reports, it's also worth noting (again, without spoilers) that just because you do have $2 million in your Buck Me savings account does not guarantee you will see this particular ending. There are still choices you'll need to make in the final mission that determine which ending you see.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I am both a bit too young and a bit too very not American to have ever experienced public-access television, but it's something that's always fascinated me. For those too young to have even heard of it, or just not in the know, it essentially allowed anyone to broadcast their own reveals through cable TV. A proto YouTube, if you will. It's obviously not what it was any more, given the advent of the internet, but in NIGHTEYE.TV, it may be making a digital, more interactive return.

It has been revealed that NIGHTEYE.TV is a strange little place. I call it a place, it's a fake TV floating in a Unity default texture void, lending it a Backroomsian vibe, but even if there's not much there to ground yourself in, the goggle box is enticing all the same. It beckons you to turn it on, a series of buttons all linking to different "channels." What awaits you isn't television, however. Instead you'll find games, mostly of the weirdo, freako, sicko variety, quickly setting the tone.

🌕NIGHT EYE TV’s initial form is live!🌑 Check out the site and follow our Indiegogo campaign at www.nighteye.tv![image or embed].

In its current incarnation, it's mostly just a collection of clips of these various art games, with direct links to them hidden away in a menu, but a good collection it is. You'll find Nathalie Lawhead's Everything is Going to Be OK, Jeremy Couillard's more recent Soul Injector Commando, and Taylor McCue's He Fucked The Girl Out Of Me. Some clips are longer than others, acting as sort of segments of playthroughs, but it all feels like an exciting evolution of what public-access television was.

The ultimate goal is for it to be a curated platform where you can buy a rotating selection of games. Most of the sale goes back to the original artist, and 15% gets put into a community pool to be split amongst all of the contributors, with the last 15% going towards keeping everything running. As it stands, that's not quite ready yet. You can help make it happen, though, as right now an Indiegogo campaign is running to help it all get fully operational. Worth chucking a few quid I reckon!

Latest Update: As Rockstar's alleged "union busting" tribunal hearing comes to a close amid GTA 6 launch, judge pledges to deliver verdict "as promptly as I possibly can"

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (402 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Closing statements in Rockstar and IWGB's employment tribunal case - revolving around the GTA 6 developer's alleged 'union busting' and the firing of 34 employees - have now been read, bringing the hearing to an end.
  • Sources indicate that the case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights.
  • In a recent development, people Makes Games' Chris Bratt has been following the case closely and reporting on proceedings as they've unfolded.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Closing statements in Rockstar and IWGB's employment tribunal case - revolving around the GTA 6 developer's alleged 'union busting' and the firing of 34 employees - have now been read, bringing the hearing to an end. There's presently no timeline for a verdict, however, with one commentator suggesting a judgement could take weeks or months to arrive.

Sources indicate that the case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights. Rockstar has been accused of unlawfully firing workers for being part of a union, but the GTA developer insists employees were dismissed for breaching confidentiality agreements.

In a recent development, people Makes Games' Chris Bratt has been following the case closely and reporting on proceedings as they've unfolded. With closing statements now complete, Bratt quoted Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying, "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as swiftly as I possibly can.".

However, Bratt suggests it could be ""anywhere from a few weeks up to a few months before we actually hear the judgement", noting "The firings themselves, let's not forget, happened over a year ago now. This has been a slog.".

One fired Rockstar worker involved in the case spoke with Bratt after the closing statements to share their thoughts. "Honestly it's just sort of blended together," they said. "It’s been so long, that after the first six months or so it became the fresh depressing reality. I'm hoping the judgement will release us from it.".

Last month, the conclusion of the tribunal hearing was delayed after cross examination of witnesses ran long.

Yesterday's closing statements come at a time when all eyes are on GTA 6 as it finally releases this week, concluding years of development for both current and former employees. Many of those workers involved in the case urged players to support the game despite the legal dispute.

Additionally, Rockstar employees are currently voting on whether they want recognised union representation at the studio. If the vote passes, it would be the largest recognised union across the entirety of the UK video game industry. The deadline for union votes is 26th November.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it's been several years since the Daniel Craig era of James Bond concluded, and work on Bond 26 is at the moment underway. Of course, this past week there was some significant news on the front, as it was finally confirmed that Robert Pattinson would play the fresh 007. All the while, many are still wondering who will be the next Bond Girl. My pick is Alexandra Daddario, and I'm not the only one who feels that way. Now, amid the rumors, Daddario is weighing in.

According to recent reports that have dropped, the race for the position of next Bond Girl is becoming quite interesting. So far, prediction market Kalshi’s got Margaret Qualley topping Sydney Sweeney for its pick, followed by names like Anya Taylor-Joy and Florence Pugh along with others. While Daddario’s not on that list, it's no surprise she's still been linked to Bond 26 speculation. While speaking to Hollywood ReelTime, the fan-favorite actress shared a level-headed take:.

Sources indicate that the internet says things. I don’t really know. (laughs) I mean, I’m very excited to see the Bond movie, but I don’t believe I’ll be in it. I don’t know. The internet can say anything, I guess.

Industry observers note that based on the Couples Weekend star's laughter throughout her response, I’m curious if she knows something we don’t. But, like her Hershey costar Finn Witrock noted, “Never say never.” I personally think Daddario would do a great job, as she has more than enough charm to pull it off. When looking back at the most iconic Bond Girls throughout history, they've each had elements of seen glamour, intelligence, emotional depth and mystery, and Daddario can embody all of those attributes.

It has been revealed that we clearly know the Mayfair Witches actress has the beauty that’ll surely make the MI6 agent swoon. Whether she's wowing us with an end-of-summer bikini or giving Hollywood glamour in a gorgeous backless dress, fashionista Daddario would be perfect for it. Not to mention, any Bond can fall under the spell of her piercing blue eyes.

It has been revealed that other than looking like a true beauty, though, the Texas Chainsaw 3D star has experience with action movies like the Percy Jackson films and San Andreas. Daddario has also played characters who are vulnerable and emotionally guarded. Through her award-recognized portrayal of Rachel in The White Lotus, she played a woman experiencing internal struggles and conflicting emotions about her husband.

Also, in True Detective, Daddario's character, Lisa, refuses to be disregarded while serving as a mistress to Detective Hart. So, with these two HBO roles alone, I believe Daddario can give both sensuality and substance while playing a Bond Girl. I also want to see her chemistry with Robert Pattinson. While the two have never done a project together, I can see them playing off each other well.

In a recent development, while we don’t know yet who will be the lucky lady to play the next Bond Girl, I'm keeping my fingers crossed for Alexandra Daddario to get the part. Hopefully, additional information on the upcoming film -- which is being directed by Denis Villeneuve -- will arrive sooner rather than later. In the meantime, though, you can watch Daddario in the 2026 movie release Hershey, which is in theaters now.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As GTA 6 finally arrives, increasingly outspoken games industry legend Warren Spector - known for seminal immersive sims including Deus Ex - has offered both praise for the game's achievements and lambasted its "billion dollar" development model, writing, "I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it’s the best we have to offer".

Spector announced his retirement from games development in August following struggles at his OtherSide Entertainment studio, and has been vocal about the state of the games industry in the months since, notably saying anyone at EA responsible for the "travesty" of BioWare's closure should be "ashamed". And now Spector has taken on GTA 6.

"First, congratulations to everyone who worked on GTA 6. It looks like it will be a high point of sorts for our medium and our business," he wrote in a post on LinkedIn. "However… its billion dollar development cost and an undoubtedly crazy marketing budget don't represent a business model anyone else can or probably should emulate.

"That's especially true," Spector continued, "when thousands of developers are out of work. A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries. Personally I'd rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is.".

In a recent development, the "sure success" of GTA 6 proves a point he's made "for years", he mentioned: "That no game that matters ships on time and/or on budget". Highlighting GTA 6's year-long delay and reported billion dollar budget, Spector suggested, "Give a game the time and money to prove its potential (key word, potential) and you have a chance of making something great. Underfund a game or force it out the door before it's ready [is] guaranteed failure no matter how much potential it has.

"So, again, congratulations," Spector concluded. "Ambition and innovation are necessary for the medium to reach its potential. I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind even if it's the best we have to offer.".

Despite Spector's concerns, GTA 6's arrival is, as expected, already causing shockwaves across the industry. It has broken pre-order records for Xbox and PlayStation stores, smashed the all-time livestream viewer record, and apparently briefly broke Reddit too. And is its success deserved? Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell thinks so, saying it "pushes back the horizon of video games once again" in his five star GTA 6 review.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Alternatively, and perhaps more enticingly, if you run something like a Plex or Jellyfin server, you can hook that up to the game too, where again all of the films you own digitally show up in store.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that since the beginning of the year, I have watched almost 150 films. I know this, because over the past few years, I've become one of those people… a Letterboxd user. Gasp! I know, I know, but I don't think I'm too insufferable about it. I'll only do a joke review in the hopes of like farming if I think it's genuinely funny! But many of these films were watched digitally, meaning I don't have a bunch of DVDs to admire on a shelf. So what am I to do? Well, I could check out Alt Video, a not quite job simulator where you can use your Letterboxd account or media server to fill up a digital, faux Blockbuster.

According to recent reports, this is, obviously, not so dissimilar to Boxroom, a game where you can design your own bedroom that lets you use your Steam profile to fill it with games you actually own. With Alt Video, you do things slightly differently just because of the focus on a different format. So, say you have a Letterboxd account. After exporting some data from your account, you can bring that into Alt Video, and this fake video store will then get filled up with shelves of DVD cases of all the films you've watched.

Alternatively, and perhaps more enticingly, if you run something like a Plex or Jellyfin server, you can hook that up to the game too, where again all of the films you own digitally show up in store. What's more interesting here is that there's a cinema room in the store that lets you watch films on your Plex server, and it's possible to invite your Steam friends to watch along with you. There's even a few other rooms, like a '90s bedroom or family room for more of a CRT kinda vibe. It's cute! If you like you can even manually add any DVDs or Blu-rays you own to appear on all the shelves too.

In a recent development, there's a lot of other nice touches too. In the case of your Letterboxd data, your ratings even show up on the back of the boxes. It's not just relegated to films either, you can put in reveals or even your games. The whole thing can be played in VR if you really want that immersive feel. There's a store clerk who can give you some recommendations if you're not sure what to watch. And there's even a day and night system, weather, and seasonal shopfront facelifts.

According to recent reports, alt Video is currently slated for release next week on November 24th, and it'll be doing so in early access. Worth noting that for now the focus is on the browsing, but features involving serving customers and running the store are on the way. You can wishlist it on Steam right here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that use of generative AI in game dev remains as contentious as it does ubiquitous—a recent GDC report found that around 40% of devs use AI, but more than half think its influence has been negative. Ubisoft is continuing to double down on the technology, this time with Motherbrain, a newly introduced subsidiary fashioned from the team behind its "first playable generative AI experience.".

As reported by VGC, Motherbrain's purpose is to develop "AI for gameplay innovation, supporting all game creators in developing groundbreaking experiences … Its current focus is on new player experiences, smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large scale systemic worlds," according to an earnings report which was released Thursday.

The information comes at a turbulent time for the publishing giant, which just laid off 166 employees even after Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced "outperformed expectations." A sweeping internal overhaul earlier this year saw the company reorganize its workforce into a throng of "creative houses," a decision which led to swathes of layoffs and six project cancellations, including the Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time Remake.

It's not clear what Motherbrain are at work on, in specific terms, right now, but there may be some clues in its past work. That playable AI "experience" I mentioned earlier is none other than Teammates, an R&D project based on a prior experiment with uncanny AI "neo-NPCs.".

Recent findings suggest that teammates aimed to allow players to command NPC squadmates in a rudimentary shooter game with a microphone, and using AI, have those squadmates react believably. It's not far off, at least conceptually, from what we've seen in games like Where Winds Meet and Fortnite, both of which have experimented with AI-powered NPCs.

Tech Report: Does GTA 6 have an 'easy mode'? Not officially, but there are two very notable settings you can change to make the game less difficult

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (561 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By now, you've probably heard that you cannot use cheats in GTA 6 until you complete the main story.
  • But, for anyone looking to have a slightly easier time with GTA 6 than the dev's intended experience, I come with good news: you can make the game a little bit easier by toggling two options in the game's Settings menu.
  • 'Accessible Combat' decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By now, you've probably heard that you cannot use cheats in GTA 6 until you complete the main story. Not only that, but enabling cheat codes also locks story progression and deactivates the ability to save. Basically, you can use cheats to have a quick crime spree and blow off some steam, then it's back to normalcy. Understandably, some gamers are a little put out with this change.

But, for anyone looking to have a slightly easier time with GTA 6 than the dev's intended experience, I come with good news: you can make the game a little bit easier by toggling two options in the game's Settings menu. If you open Settings, and then navigate to Gameplay, you'll find 'Accessible Combat' and 'Reduced Vehicle Damage' toggles. You can activate both to make GTA 6's more difficult elements a little bit easier to work through.

'Accessible Combat' decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider. 'Reduced Vehicle Damage', as you'd expect, lowers the damage taken by your vehicle and allows your ride to endure more punishment. This applies to gunfire, environmental threats, and impact damage.

In a recent development, toggle these settings comes with a warning from Rockstar, though. A prompt notes that enabling these modifiers will "significantly change the balance and experience of the gameplay". I've been playing around with these settings and whilst they are not a foolproof 'God Mode' by any means, you can absolutely see a difference in the game when they're enabled: Jason and Lucia take a lot more punishment from melee damage and gunshots, and I had to really try to get Jason's old banged up pickup into even the 'slightly smoking' bracket of disrepair. Your mileage may vary, but these settings, from what I can tell so far, certainly do make the game easier.

Recent findings suggest that given that cheats disable trophies and progression, these settings might be something to keep in mind if you're trying to find a smoother path through the main story of GTA 6. It's a credit to Rockstar's accessibility teams that these have been included at all - alongside the 23 other gameplay accessibility options, the 12 display options, the 70 UI options, the 24 camera options, and the 14 audio options.

Sources indicate that "We create inclusive, intuitive, and immersive experiences for every player," noted Rockstar's associate UI director, Sam Grosset, in materials provided to Eurogamer ahead of the game's launch. "Accessibility is considered from the outset, and designing for diverse needs enables us to create better games for everyone. We wanted every player in GTA 6 to have options to play the game how they like. Whether it's selecting a larger font size, opting for a more minimal screen experience, or making a controls tweak to sprinting... the choices are open to all.".

We also learned yesterday that Rockstar has made GTA 6 missions "harder to fail" by making them more open-ended, and giving players more ways to figure out how to do things in their own way.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some GTA 6 hopefuls weren't chuffed when hearing the open-world crime fest is targeting 30fps on all consoles, but there's actually a way to circumvent that framerate cap thanks to a newly-discovered glitch on Xbox.

Before the game's meteoric launch, Rockstar Games confirmed that its crime fest was locked at 30fps on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S - the studio acknowledged that even the PS5 Pro wasn't capable enough to simulate the game's massive, complicated world at higher framerates, either.

But Redditor Mewwie64's has found a way to run the game with an unlocked framerate by using a Quick Resume glitch on Xbox Series X - that's the handy feature that lets you switch between games from where you last left off, without needing to boot up each one from scratch.

It has been revealed that to run GTA 6 at 60fps or higher, you'll apparently need a 120hz display, an Xbox Series X, and the game itself on version 01.002.001. "This glitch may still work on later versions," the Redditor indicates, "not sure.".

The dedicated player also gave interested folks a tutorial on how to up those framerate caps: "Put your Xbox display settings to 60hz. Start GTA 6. Wait until you see the six stars in the intro. Change your display settings back to 120hz. Cold boot another game on your console via the Xbox Guide (The Xbox button) and without quitting GTA 6. Switch back to GTA 6." And, voila.

It has been revealed that the Redditor does have one pretty big disclaimer, before you get too excited. "The game speed seems to be tied to your framerate," they write, so increasing the framerate might lead to certain animations looking faster than normal.

It has been revealed that "It seems like the animations are at 2x speed or more in Jason's house in Chapter 1. I have a stable 90fps and everything works fine but Jason's animations run at 2x speed or more. But when you exit the house everything runs at an increased speed (The game world is likely tied to your framerate) but cutscenes work 100% fine without issues on higher framerates. Only the gameplay is sped up." Be warned, then.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto VI came out on November 19, and literally one day after that, it was announced that it had hit $3.79 billion in sales.
  • To get into the specifics, it was reported by Rockstar Games that GTA VI has reached $3.79 billion in sales as of November 20, per The AP.
  • Industry observers note that looking at the Eras Tour, specifically, after its 21-month run, it racked up $2 billion in tickets sold and over 10 million people attended the concerts (its proshot was also a major box office success and can now be streamed with a Disney+ subscription).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto VI came out on November 19, and literally one day after that, it was announced that it had hit $3.79 billion in sales. That’s a seriously impressive number. I mean, it took Taylor Swift nearly two years to make $2 billion with her highly profitable Eras Tour. GTA did more than that in one day. However, while that is quite mind-blowing to think about, fans aren’t so impressed by this comparison.

To get into the specifics, it was reported by Rockstar Games that GTA VI has reached $3.79 billion in sales as of November 20, per The AP. It also stated that 32.5 million units were sold in pre-release. When People published a story on what the video game had reportedly made, it prominently noted that it had already outgrossed Taylor Swift’s Eras Tour.

Industry observers note that looking at the Eras Tour, specifically, after its 21-month run, it racked up $2 billion in tickets sold and over 10 million people attended the concerts (its proshot was also a major box office success and can now be streamed with a Disney+ subscription). The NYT, that’s “double the gross ticket sales of any other concert tour in history.” Also, reportedly, the tour’s average gross per night was between $14 and $17 million.

Industry observers note that considering the fact that both the Eras Tour and GTA VI were highly anticipated events – Taylor Swift hadn’t toured in six years before Eras, and fans waited 13 years for the new GTA – I get why this comparison is staggering. It’s honestly wild that it took GTA one day to do more than what Taylor Swift did in a little less than two years.

However, many fans made it clear they weren’t that impressed by this comparison.

When you really think about it, comparing GTA to the Eras Tour is like comparing apples and oranges. One is a concert tour; the other is a video game. Yes, they’re both major moments of monoculture. However, that’s kind of all they have in common. So, that left people commenting things like this on People’s post about the video game outgrossing Swift’s tour:.

Something many comments pointed out was that there was a cap on how many people could attend the Eras Tour. There are only so many people you can fit in a stadium. Anyone can buy and play Grand Theft Auto VI. So, it makes sense that it could make more than the tour in such a short period of time.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

It might be more fitting to compare GTA VI's release to this year’s box office, considering almost anyone can go to the movies if they want to. In one day, this video game managed to make more than the current highest-grossing film on the 2026 movie schedule, which is Spider-Man: Brand Fresh Day (the film made more than $2 billion worldwide during its run in theaters this summer).

Then, if we really want to compare apples to apples, Grand Theft Auto V generated $1 billion in sales during its first three days. In total, the 2013 game accounts for over 230 million of the franchise's 470 million units sold. It would seem the sixth installment is well on its way to beating its predecessor.

Anyway, getting back to GTA and The Eras Tour, overall, I agree with fans in a way, because this is a hard comparison to make. However, it’s also undeniable that the release of GTA VI and The Eras Tour are two of the biggest pop culture moments in recent history, and it is kind of wild that the video game managed to outgross the concert series in one day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that we already knew there'd be a frantic clamour for GTA 6 this week, and we also knew plenty of players would be eyeing up Xbox's 'New Zealand trick' to get in on the action early. But it's now being reported that a whopping 2m UK and US players took advantage of the trick - which, for context, equals more than a third of New Zealand's actual population.

Here's a quick bit of background: Rockstar's regional release schedule meant GTA 6 debuted at midnight on 19th November everywhere, local time. As such, New Zealand was the first country in the world to see the hugely anticipated game go live, thanks to timezones. And because Xbox players can make purchases on any regional store easily, simply by changing their console's country, understandably impatient sorts opted to become temporary virtual New Zealand residents in their droves (on PlayStation, the process requires a regional account and payment in local currency so is more finicky).

Industry observers note that in fact, according to data analytics firm Ampere Analysis, the early demand was such that 1.5m Xbox owners in the US and 600,000 UK Xbox players briefly went Kiwi for the occasion of GTA 6's launch. Other countries highlighted by Ampere include Canada, where 200,000 Xbox players took the Fresh Zealand plunge, Brazil (200,000 players), and Mexico (100,000 players).

By contrast, just 100,000 PlayStation players in the US opted to dive in early, reflecting, as Ampere notes, "the ease of being able to switch country in the account settings on Xbox consoles." And here's all that info in graph form:.

Amusingly, Upcoming Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Sources indicate that some hours later and the rest of the world can now finally, officially join in the GTA 6 fun, and it's a game worth playing. Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell called it an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in his five star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Upgrading your TV's sound doesn't necessarily mean spending a fortune on a full home theater setup, especially with early Black Friday deals bringing substantial discounts on soundbars and audio systems from Sony, Bose, Samsung, and LG. Sony has some of the biggest price cuts, with savings of up to 32% across select Bravia Theater models, including more than $700 off its premium Theater Trio system.

Recent findings suggest that samsung's Dolby Atmos soundbars are also discounted by as much as $400, while Bose and LG have more affordable options for anyone looking to improve dialogue clarity, add some bass, or enjoy surround sound without a complicated setup. Whether you're shopping for a compact speaker for a bedroom TV or a more immersive system for movie nights, here are the deals worth considering.

Industry observers note that for anyone building a premium home theater around a large TV, the Sony Bravia Theater Trio is down to $1,498 from $2,199.99, saving you $701.99, or roughly 32%. Unlike a conventional soundbar, the Trio uses three separate front speakers for the left, center, and right channels, helping spread dialogue and effects across a wider soundstage. You can read PCMag’s “excellent” review for more details.

Recent findings suggest that the Sony Bravia Theater Bar 7 is down to $718 from $869 for anyone who wants a single soundbar under the TV. Its nine speakers include upward- and side-firing drivers that widen the soundstage and give Dolby Atmos some height, but there’s no subwoofer, so the now $898 Bar 7 with a wireless sub bundle (down from $1,099.99) might be the better pick for deeper bass.

According to recent reports, moving down Sony's lineup, the Bravia Theater Bar 6 is $548, down from $699.99, and pairs a 3.1.2-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer and upward-firing speakers for Dolby Atmos height effects. Spending $100 more gets you the Bravia Theater System 6, now $648 from $799.99, which adds rear speakers in a 5.1-channel setup for movies and games where sound moves behind you.

For a more affordable upgrade, the Sony Bravia Theater Bar 5 is down to $278 from $349.99, saving you nearly $72. It's a 3.1-channel system with a dedicated center speaker and wireless subwoofer, so dialogue should come through more clearly while music and movie effects get some additional low-end presence.

Recent findings suggest that sony’s older systems are discounted too, including the HT-S400 at $258, down from $299, which pairs a 2.1-channel soundbar and wireless subwoofer with S-Force Pro Front Surround to widen the sound for everyday TV, sports, and casual movies. The HT-S40R is arguably the better deal at the same $258, down from $329.99, since it adds two rear speakers for a full 5.1-channel setup, though neither model supports Dolby Atmos.

It has been revealed that for smaller rooms or for anyone who mainly wants dialogue to come across more clearly, Bose has two compact soundbars on sale: The newer Bose TV Speaker (2nd Gen) is down to $239 from $299, with an updated acoustic design that Bose states improves clarity and overall sound performance. Meanwhile, the original Bose TV Speaker is $199, down from $279, and offers a similarly compact design with a dedicated dialogue mode and adjustable bass.

Samsung’s HW-Q800H is down to $697.99 from $1,097.99, a $400 cut on a 5.1.2-channel Dolby Atmos soundbar with a wireless subwoofer. Its side- and upward-firing speakers help place effects around and above you, while a dedicated center channel keeps dialogue clear during busy action scenes.

Industry observers note that for something that takes up less space, the Samsung HW-S60D is $277.99, down from $399.99, and fits seven speakers, including side-firing drivers, into a compact 5.0-channel soundbar. It also supports Dolby Atmos, Adaptive Sound, and a voice enhancement mode, along with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, AirPlay, and Chromecast for music streaming. That stated, it has no upward-firing speakers or subwoofer, so its height effects and bass won’t match that of the Q800H.

According to recent reports, if you're looking for a complete surround sound system without spending several hundred dollars, the LG S6FTR is down to $249.99 from $399.99, saving you $150, or roughly 38%. It's a 5.1-channel home theater package with a soundbar, subwoofer, and dedicated rear speakers. That makes it particularly appealing for action movies and games, where directional sound adds to the experience.

The LG S40TR is another affordable option for anyone who wants rear speakers included in the box. It's presently $199.99, down from $279.99, and offers a 4.1-channel arrangement with a wireless subwoofer and two rear speakers. This should give movie soundtracks a greater sense of direction than a basic soundbar, while the subwoofer handles the lower frequencies that smaller TV speakers often struggle to reproduce.

At just under $187, the S60T is the least expensive system in this roundup, pairing a 3.1-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer for clearer dialogue and fuller sound than your TV’s speakers. That mentioned, it lacks rear speakers and Dolby Atmos height channels, so it’s better suited to someone who wants a simple, affordable upgrade without filling the room with additional hardware.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

Sources indicate that black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was better for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, do your research, or refer to guides like our Black Friday and Cyber Monday coverage that have done all the vetting for you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, actor Andrew Scott is synonymous with playing Hot Priest in Fleabag (streaming with an Amazon Prime subscription), but he's a versatile star of the screen and stage. Those two worlds combine in the upcoming LGBTQ+ movie Elsinore, directed by Simone Stone. The biographical drama film tells the story of late actor Ian Charleson, who performed the title role of Hamlet at the National Theatre while secretly struggling with AIDS in the midst of the AIDS crisis. The movie is endlessly powerful, and I have so many thoughts as someone who comes from the theatre.

I'm a proud theater kid, one who is still acting and producing to this day in the community theater space. While I loved Andrew Scott's stunning performance in Elsinore and the way it honored Charleson and the countless queer folks that we lost to the AIDS crisis, I was also taken by how accurately the fresh film portrayed what it's like to work in theater... warts and all.

Industry observers note that while Club Kid is my favorite movie of the year (so far), Elsinore is another LGBTQ+ story that I feel privileged to have seen. The movie tells the real-life story of Ian Charleson struggling with AIDS while also preparing to play the behemoth role of Hamlet at the National Theatre. It's a truly gut-wrenching story, told expertly through the film's 111-minute runtime. Throughout the movie, I was shook by how seen I felt by the way it portrayed working on a theater production.

To start, there was the almost neurotic way that Ian is shown preparing to play the titular character Hamlet. We see him working long hours in the sparse rehearsal room, where experimentation and heeding notes from director Richard Eyre transformed his performance from a piece of marble into a detailed statue. While stage actors make this look easy, there is way more work than casual audiences might grasp from their seat in the house.

Then there was the process of line memorization. Ian is shown drilling lines pretty much non-stop throughout Elsinore, including when he's getting treatments and even while recovering after being hospitalized. This rings so true to me; if I'm in a dialogue-heavy play, I function in the same way. For instance, when I played Prior Walter in Tony Kushner's Angels in America, I couldn't stop drilling my lines. That includes testing myself with flashcards, as well as repeating my monologues every time I was in the shower and/or driving in the car.

Much like Ian in Elsinore, getting those lines ingrained in my head allows for more freedom and expression during performances, rather than searching for what comes next in my head.

Then there's the sense of community that's shown in the new movie. While Ian spends most of the movie hiding his diagnosis, he eventually tells them the truth before opening night. He expected judgment, but his colleagues swiftly accept him and offer support for his performance. This feels very true to the experience of being in the theater; weird chosen families often form with each production. I've seen ensembles rally around people struggling with grief, miscarriages, election results and more.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Overall, it really felt like Elsinore was created by folks who knew and love what it means to work in the theater. Obviously this isn't the point of the movie per se, but it's one of many reasons why I thought it was so incredible.

Recent findings suggest that elsinore is in theaters now as part of the 2026 movie release list. Word to the wise: bring your tissues.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No matter how far you're through the main GTA 6 missions list, you are probably starting to get a sense of just how massive Leonida really is – and how stacked it is with curiosities, distractions, objectives, and side-activities. So naturally you must be wondering if you can free-roam after beating GTA 6, or whether you need to pack everything in before hitting a point of no return.

I'm going to answer this question for you and, because I'm nice, I'm going to do so in the most spoiler-free way that I possibly can.

Industry observers note that you can continue free-roam after beating GTA 6, albeit with a few caveats. Because there are numerous GTA 6 endings, with a wide range of different variables and impacts for all of the characters depending on your relationship status, your criminal profile, whether you paid into family savings, and plenty more besides, Rockstar has decided that it would be far too difficult to simply drop you back into Vice City in a world in which there are no more main missions daunting your GTA 6 Index.

According to recent reports, this means that once you've completed the main story in GTA 6, the game will drop you back to an auto-save just before the point-of-no-return. When the game does this, I recommend that you be prepared to make a new save in GTA 6 – as that auto-save won't exist forever, and can be lost if you decide to load an old save or start the campaign over from scratch.

From this point, you're free to do whatever you want to do. Your relationship status will be locked, so there's no need to worry about maintaining this if you don't want to, but you can still mess around with your Criminal Profile. You can also, at any point, restart the final mission and go through it again.

Industry observers note that the GTA 6 end-game is where the world really lets you be free. You'll have loads of GTA 6 challenges to complete, which contribute to the unlocking of GTA 6 Cheats that are now available in the Progress menu. So, long story short, you can free-roam after beating GTA 6, but expect to have that final mission sitting on your menu screen for the long haul.
