#120207. Latest Update: The making of GTA 5: How the GTA 6 predecessor helped Rockstar pave the way for its return to Vice City with Jason and Lucia

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2287 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gamesradar ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: The making of GTA 5: How the GTA 6 predecessor helped Rockstar pave the way for its return to Vice City with Jason and Lucia

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2287 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Back in 2013, Grand Theft Auto 5 won the prestigious title of Edge Magazine's Game of the Year.
  • Industry observers note that garbut's firmly looking in the rear-view mirror - back in 2013, GTA 6 would be more than a decade away, and Red Dead Redemption 2 would likely have been a much bigger concern for Rockstar.
  • How did having three playable characters inform your design choices when it came to building the world?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Back in 2013, Grand Theft Auto 5 won the prestigious title of Edge Magazine's Game of the Year. A lot has changed since then, but at least one figure is the same. Aaron Garbut, co-studio head at Rockstar North on GTA 6, was art director on GTA 5, and he spoke to Edge about the process of making that game. With GTA 6 likely to be a mainstay in Game of the Year conversations through 2027, and our own GTA 6 review out in the wild, we're revisiting that interview to see which design philosophies have stayed the same over the past 13 years, and where Rockstar's ideas have differed.

Industry observers note that garbut's firmly looking in the rear-view mirror - back in 2013, GTA 6 would be more than a decade away, and Red Dead Redemption 2 would likely have been a much bigger concern for Rockstar. But a lot of what he talks about is relevant today; the design impact of having multiple lead characters; the need to kill your darlings throughout development; the struggles of creating a realistic, life-like urban game environment. We've been sharing some of those stories this week, but you can read the full interview with Garbut right here.

How did having three playable characters inform your design choices when it came to building the world?

The world is always designed before the game. That’s just the way we do things. We have a chunk of preproduction where a subset of the art team lay out and build a white box city. We get the roads feeling good, the vistas working well and look at the skyline and landmarks. We spend a long time driving and building and tweaking and getting everything in place and feeling balanced, making sure the districts we have chosen will blend together naturally and as a whole create the feeling of the city. As missions and story come together, I work with the level designers to place missions and key locations and to utilise as much of the world as we can.

According to recent reports, we did know the [biographies] for the three characters right at the start, so we knew we wanted to create an area for Trevor out in the sticks. Towards the beginning of preproduction, I met up with [Rockstar president] Sam [Houser] in LA, and we spent a week together driving about, just exploring and talking. During that trip, we drove out into the desert and eventually ended up visiting Salton Sea [in California]. We went to an amazing spot called Bombay Beach and expected a real-life Trevor to burst out on us at any second. When the full reference trip was organised, we sent a team out to Salton Sea for a few days.

According to recent reports, with GTA Online planned as such a large part of the experience, and one which we knew we wanted to sustain, we really didn’t have the luxury of focusing solely on the singleplayer journey. We had to ensure that the world as a whole was coherent and of consistent quality. We also knew we wanted to give the entire world a sense of life, and to encourage and reward the player for exploring. I think if this was a linear experience, the three characters would have had a bigger impact on the design and workload of the world.

It has been revealed that as it was, though, they just gave us a few anchor points. All the things that hung off of that – the contrasts, the fidelity and detail, the personality – we would have done anyway. At a certain point, the detail and scope is just so massive that you can do what you want within it and it has little impact on production.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

What were the most valuable lessons you’d learnt through previous GTAs that were transferable to this project?

Mostly not to get locked down to anything, whether it’s a process, a blueprint, a goal, an asset, an idea – anything. To keep completely open-minded, adapt to the situation and always look for a better way forward, rather than stick with what’s been decided previously. I don’t mean chop and change for the sake of it, but let what’s best for the game dictate the way forward. With a game that’s as large and complex as this, the ideas need to be fluid, and you need to be paying as much attention as you can to every aspect to make sure they’re working together.

We’ve got an amazing art team here that is extremely experienced at building open worlds. We’ve been doing it for 15 years, so a lot of the problems and solutions are just so ingrained in us that we don’t really notice them. There’s always latest things that come along, though, and the nature of how we approach development means that we need to be ready to adapt. The world is built first, then missions, then structure and story, and all the time all our systems are developing and changing. Each of these things influences the others massively, so each needs to adapt to the others. We are always playing and refining, adjusting each element of the game to play better with the others. We’re rarely throwing away content; it’s more about adapting plans and constantly looking ahead with a clean slate, rather than sticking stubbornly to old decisions.

According to recent reports, I always think of the process the same way I was taught in art college to draw or sculpt. It’s about sketching in the overall vision and then layering and working in additional detail, pulling the end result out of the page. It’s just that we have a thousand people all drawing at once on the same page. We’re lucky – a lot of us have been doing this together for so long that we know how to work together.

"Multiple characters was a leap of faith" - Many years before Jason and Lucia would lead GTA 6, Rockstar knew that GTA 5's trio "might backfire". Thankfully, they seem to have dodged that particular.

Looking back, how do you think the final version of the game matches up to your initial vision?

Recent findings suggest that it’s hard to remember the original vision now. We always have a very basic idea of what we want to achieve, but from day one it’s evolving and adapting. As a game, the initial vision is always very rough. We decided right at the start we wanted to do three switchable characters, we decided who the main characters were and we decided the general tone for the game. Then we just built and evolved and let the game dictate itself.

[Having] multiple characters was a leap of faith. It was an interesting idea, and it felt like we could do interesting things with it, but it also felt like a change to the core of the game that might backfire. I think it really worked out. It’s so hard during development to get perspective – you get so used to looking for the problems that it becomes almost impossible to step back and see the positives. On this project, despite living in that world for years, playing the missions again and again, it felt fun. It felt great to experience the world, to see it evolve from the basic building blocks to the finished detailed results with all the scenarios and life added. I still think of it like a real place in a lot of ways. That’s an amazing thing – to build what feels like a real place and then for nearly 30 million people to live there.

As a group of people, we’re never short of ideas. There are always things that come up during development that you want to add. Often we do, but the closer you get to release, the less that happens. I don’t feel like the game fell short, but there is undoubtedly a huge volume of plans and ideas that we wanted to do to push it further.

What I love about our GTA Online plans is that the game is no longer static. We can continue to add these things and evolve. That’s even more exciting these days, where through forums, Reddit, etc, we have a real direct connection to the people playing the game. We can respond to what they are into and what they hate more than ever. It’s something that really suits the way we work, the way we’re always trying to adapt to the experience and avoid walking blindly down a set path.

"Let what's best for the game dictate the way forward" - Garbut notes that the most important Rockstar learned over the course of the GTA series was to kill its darlings, and be prepared to cut anything that might need to go for the good of the game.

Los Santos is the series’ closest analogy to a real location – how does that affect how it’s designed?

We always use the same process: working with real cities, starting on a macro level to define the districts we want to use, and working down. I think the only variation is how many real landmarks we decide to use once we get to the individual building level. I always feel we build our own world – we’re still a long way from being dictated by reality. Instead, we use it as a starting point. We’ll move entire districts about geographically, never mind individual buildings.

It has been revealed that I’d never want to rebuild a city. I think that would be a lot less satisfying both for us to build and for the player to play. In a lot of ways, it would be less convincing, too. At least that’s how I rationalise it to myself. Only a relatively small subset of players ever get to know the real LA or New York. Most experience it through film and TV, or through short visits, and that’s a highly edited representation. We do the same: we take the feel of a city, the one we get through visiting and through experiencing it our whole lives through media, and build that. We compress, we edit, we emphasise certain things and we end up with something that in some ways, I think, feels more like the popular perception of the place than the actual city. Only because the popular perception isn’t the real city, if that makes sense.

"I'd never want to rebuild a city, I think that would be a lot less satisfying" - Garbut says that the act of recreating a world brick-by-brick wouldn't work for either the developers or the players.

The game’s lighting system works really hard to evoke moods – how vital do you think it is to the finished game?

Recent findings suggest that it’s absolutely vital. Good lighting makes all the difference; it’s what binds the experience together. We have an extremely good lighting team who have worked together to push and push what was previously possible. It’s a hell of a lot of work and tuning, held together by extremely optimal and clever code with a layer of hacky tricks over the top to give us the things that shouldn’t be possible.

Sam Houser once told us that recreating neon lighting in Vice City was an vital breakthrough during its development. Were there equivalent points while making GTAIV and V?

It has been revealed that on IV, that was when the lighting – and in particular the realtime shadows – came online. That was a revelation for us at the time, having spent years on PS2 baking in static lighting. Suddenly, everything felt solid. On V, it was similar: the lighting system was reworked and we had a system that could draw much nicer shadows over much farther distances. The first time I saw the shadows drawing all the way into the distance while flying over the city was one of those moments – and then when the lighting [level of detail] system came together, we suddenly had a world that seemed so much more alive at night. From your position as art director, which part of creating the game was the most enjoyable? I love working with level design. As we’re laying out the world and blocking it in, we’re considering gameplay and coming up with mission ideas. I always do my best to push those ideas through, but I think the most enjoyable part of the project is when we start to place everything in the world. Once the locations are in place and level designers start to get everything to flow together and the cutscenes plugging in, it ticks over from being a series of disconnected elements into a game. It’s at this point – once everything is in place, to some degree – that the work actually starts. It’s that last chunk when you make the hard decisions, where elements that are not working have to be changed and where you can iterate. It’s hard. It takes a long time. But it’s the bit that makes all the difference. I’m not entirely sure if it’s the most enjoyable, but it’s certainly the most rewarding.

Edge magazine was released in 1993 with a mission to dig deep into the inner workings of the international videogame industry, promptly building a reputation for next-level analysis, features, interviews and reviews that holds fast nearly 30 years on.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the final weeks of Dancing with the Stars always feature really tough eliminations. However, the last few on the 2026 TV schedule have been brutal. Specifically, Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson went home during the semifinals after getting perfect scores for their Paso Doble and Glee-themed Quickstep. Now, co-host Alfonso Ribeiro has opened up about the conversation he had with the pair following their shocking elimination, and I'm feeling emotional all over again.

It has been revealed that while Jenna and Harry were always at the top of the leaderboard and felt like frontrunners on DWTS Season 35, clearly, the fans wanted the other couples in the finale more. During a conversation with TV Insider, Ribeiro shared his thoughts on this, and the conversation he had with the pro and Glee actor after they found out they’d be going home. He noted:.

There was a lot of sharing of disappointment in my heart, what they did right, and just letting them know that I care and that I’m saddened for them. Or with them. I’ll leave it at that.

I’m also saddened for them. While Harry and Jenna always had some of the best routines of every episode, their DWTS journey was plagued by some controversy and intense online discourse. Of course, there was liftgate, which led to a comment from Johnson’s husband and fellow pro Val Chmerkovskiy that got him suspended from the show for a week. There was also the ongoing debate regarding the amount of dance experience Harry Shum Jr. had before doing DWTS.

However, while Jenna and Harry’s elimination hurt, and Ribeiro spent time talking with them about it, he also noted that no matter what the outcome, the last elimination was going to be painful. It’s the last one before the finale; it would have been heartbreaking no matter who got sent home, as he stated:.

Sources indicate that going into the night, we know that all six of them … we’re going to break hearts with one going home. It wouldn’t have mattered whose name was called. There’d be controversy. There would be, ‘This is a shocking elimination.’ It was going to be that the last several weeks, no matter what, because this for the first time, I think in this show’s history, there were eight people who ultimately could win this show this season for many different reasons. And that’s not normally the case.

Industry observers note that it does feel like the mirrorball trophy could be anyone's. They’re all pretty good, and it’s clear that everyone left has a very devoted fan base. So, it’s unclear who will win, and an argument can be made for any of them. I mean, when I think about all this, there’s part of me that wants Amber Glenn to win, and thinks she can do it based on her scores and consistency. Meanwhile, Connor Wood’s social media likes prove he has a very devoted group of fans behind him that could help make up for his lower scores and push him across the finish line. Seriously, it’s anyone’s game.

So, it made sense that Ribeiro said this in the wake of Jenna and Harry’s elimination:.

Recent findings suggest that there’s ultimate shock every time the person’s name comes up on that card, and also a bit of sadness. Because regardless of who you might think [should go] on and any of that, the reality is that they’ve all put their heart and soul into doing this. They put their lives and their families … they put it all on the back burner while trying to deliver these performances.

I totally see his point. DWTS is a massive time commitment, and it’s an intense experience both physically and mentally. These stars put their everything into it, and so it’s sad to see any of them not reach the end.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Industry observers note that however, at the end of the day, this is a competition, and ultimately only one couple can win. To see who takes home the mirrorball, you can catch the finale of Dancing with the Stars this Tuesday, November 24, on ABC or with a Disney+ subscription at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT, as it will air live on both coasts.

Five Hacks Every Apple Watch Series 12 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (808 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the latest Apple Watches have a lot of newly introduced features that older watches don't, so I figured it was time for a new list of hacks.
  • The Series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest Apple Watch models.
  • You don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the latest Apple Watches have a lot of newly introduced features that older watches don't, so I figured it was time for a new list of hacks. While our general Apple Watch and fitness tracking hacks are still golden, Series 12 devices offer new features like native step counting, a Readiness app, an upgraded heart rate sensor, an AI-based version of Siri, and "audio intelligence" that can replay and summarize real-life conversations, within limits. Here's how to get the most out of them.

The Series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest Apple Watch models. Enjoy it! To add a step counter to your watch face, long-press on the clock screen to edit it, tap on a complication (that’s what Apple calls those little icons and numbers that appear on some watch faces), choose Activity, and then tap Steps.

You don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion. A button in your Apple Watch’s Control Center can turn the feature on and off. Keep it off except when you have a structured conversation that you’ll want to refer to later. This feature is right now in beta (which you can try now if you want to), but is expected to be available to everyone later this year.

It's worth turning off the default setting not just because of the creepiness factor, but also because the recaps work best when there is a single subject of conversation, with a clear start and end, and just one context. If you leave recaps running all the time, your doctor’s appointment will get mixed in with your grocery shopping, YouTube watching, and everyday chatter.

In a recent development, to finish off a recap and make it useful, take a look at the recap shortly after the conversation, tap the three-dots menu, and hit Edit. You’ll be able to adjust the notes and add your own notable details. Siri won’t identify speakers and seems to shy away from including certain details, like people’s names. You can add in what it missed and also create your own bullet points so that everything gets noted down while it’s still fresh in your mind.

This one isn’t specific to the Series 12, but if you haven’t gotten on board with the pinch and wrist flick gestures yet, now is a great time.

It has been revealed that first, the wrist flick: If a notification is on your screen, or you’re otherwise looking at something you’d rather be done with, just flick your wrist away from you and then back toward you, as if there were a crumb on the watch face and you wanted to knock it off. This will bring you back to the watch face and close whatever you were looking at.

The double pinch is another useful one, although Apple calls it double tap. This is confusing because you aren’t double tapping the watch, you’re tapping your thumb and forefinger together while wearing the watch. You don’t need to touch the watch face at all. So, when you get a notification or a call, look at it on your watch, and pinch your thumb and forefinger (of the watch hand) together twice. The watch detects the pinch from subtle movements in your wrist, and it will open the notification. You can then use the wrist flick to close the notification. Performing a double pinch when no notification is on screen will bring up your smart stack. You can then double-pinch to move to the next card in the smart stack, or single-pinch to open that card and see its details.

Industry observers note that if you want to learn even more gestures, go into the Watch app, and select Accessibility and then Hand gestures. You can remap a whole-fist “clench” to do the same thing as pressing the digital crown, for example, or to open the control center or Siri.

Sources indicate that A little rude, perhaps, but helpful: With the upcoming AI-based Siri, sometimes answers to questions can be long-winded. If Siri rolls out into a novel-length response and you’re not interested in hearing all that, just put your palm over the screen. You’ll instantly be transported back to your watch face, and the Siri response will stop.

If you still want to see those longer responses without having Siri read the whole thing to you, you can set this up on your phone, and the settings will carry over to your watch. On your iPhone, go to Settings and tap Siri, then Responses. Select Silent responses instead of Spoken responses. You can then read through her answers, or skim them, as you prefer.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • "I can FINALLY share that I play the first-ever nonbinary character in the Grand Theft Auto franchise!" Rose wrote on Instagram.
  • "Absolutely wild to find out THIS was the super-secret game I spent weeks and 17 NDAs filming 3 years ago.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 features the first non-binary character in the series' history, according to actor Jesse James Rose, who plays the role of a museum curator in the game.

"I can FINALLY share that I play the first-ever nonbinary character in the Grand Theft Auto franchise!" Rose wrote on Instagram.

"Absolutely wild to find out THIS was the super-secret game I spent weeks and 17 NDAs filming 3 years ago.".

It has been revealed that "I shot this back in my they/them days, and everyone on production ensured I was comfortable and gendered correctly," Rose wrote. The project was kept so secret that Rose wasn't told what it was during filming and only recently learned it was GTA 6.

"GTA was one of the most inclusive & caring sets I've ever been on," they added.

A post shared by Jesse James Rose ✨ (@jamesissmiling).

Industry observers note that the role was shot entirely through motion capture, which meant wearing "a unitard made of dots every day". Rose also says steps were taken to protect the character in-game: "To mitigate anti-trans violence, I was assured that players would not be able to inflict violence against my character.".

A whole day of the shoot was spent scanning Rose's face, including hours of pulling different expressions. At one point Rose couldn't move a particular muscle, and worried the scan had been ruined, but the director was thrilled.

Recent findings suggest that "That right there is exactly why we'll never use AI," he noted, according to Rose. "A computer could never come up with the face you just made.".

"Remember, in a world consumed with Generative AI, the largest video game in history chose human labour to preserve the integrity of the game," Rose added.

Rose did raise some concerns about pay, though.

"Despite being paid well for my time on set, I'll never see a residual check for my work," Rose wrote, explaining that this is part of SAG’s contract with game developers. As a union leader at one of SAG's sister unions, Rose noted there's still "a long way to go to ensure arts workers are fairly compensated for our labour".

Rose also claims many other trans people worked on GTA 6, both in front of the camera and behind it. "SO many trans people besides me are featured in GTA VI as other roles, designers, writers, etc... take a note, theatre and TV! We are employable & profitable!!!".

In a recent development, finally, Rose voiced support for Rockstar's UK staff. "UK-based workers at Rockstar Games are right now voting on whether to unionise, and I sincerely hope their efforts are successful," Rose wrote. "Every arts worker should have a stable job with benefits and fair working conditions protected by a union.".

GTA 6 is out now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It released on Thursday, although some have been getting in on the action earlier, as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even New Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I often find myself thinking where the best place to survive a zombie apocalypse would be.
  • In a recent development, you do just this in The Road of Dust and Sorrow's demo, although it's certainly not as whimsical as I first imagined it to be.
  • Industry observers note that this isn't an easy task.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I often find myself thinking where the best place to survive a zombie apocalypse would be. A walled-off stone house would certainly make for some good defenses, a boat would be great—but only if the zombies didn't pull a Fear the Walking Dead—or you could spend the end of the world in a camper van. That would certainly be whimsical.

In a recent development, you do just this in The Road of Dust and Sorrow's demo, although it's certainly not as whimsical as I first imagined it to be. You see, in this 2D horror game you have bigger responsibilities than just keeping yourself alive, you also have a young daughter to look out for as well.

Industry observers note that this isn't an easy task. Supplies are dwindling, zombie-like humans infected by addictive chemicals amble across the land in search of more dust, but they'll settle for your blood instead. Plus there's this creepy Pastor who's definitely up to something very bad. I only got one glimpse of him in the demo and he was surrounded by a lot of gore and eldritch horror, so I've just decided that staying away from him is probably for the best.

But you can't hunker down and forget about all these terrors, because you have a daughter to feed and protect. So I spent most of my time in the demo gathering food, medical supplies, and trying to locate an item that may just grant us safe passage to the only sanctuary humanity has left.

The dev, Painted Black Games, says it took inspiration from horror series like Silent Hill and Resident Evil for The Road of Dust and Sorrow, and while I haven't come across anything particularly traumatic in a Silent Hill sense yet (although I wouldn't be surprised to see that here) I can see the through line to Resident Evil.

The action is smooth, accurate, and rewarding—which surprised me as I usually don't vibe with 2D gunplay, sometimes the controls are too finicky, but it certainly works here. Head-shotting the zombies is incredibly satisfying, as is kicking them to the floor and beating them with a baseball bat.

Then there are the puzzles. I didn't come across too many, but the ones I did find were very rewarding. It's not rocket science, but the solutions aren't always obvious either. They are, however, very intuitive; you can do a lot with a little, something I very much appreciate.

Keep up to date with the most notable stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Sources indicate that but my favourite aspect of The Road of Dust and Sorrow has to be just how cool this post-apocalyptic world is. Maybe it's the pixel art, but it manages to look dilapidated and creepy while also being oddly pretty to look at. I was searching an abandoned warehouse full of zombies and rotting cargo while thinking to myself that with a bit of elbow grease this place could really scrub up.

If you want pretty and cosy, though, the campervan is where it's at. I didn't spend as much time as I would have liked to there, but it managed to feel like a real home—the only safe place left in this world.

Tech Report: 10 Hacks Every watchOS 27 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1342 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • watchOS 27 introduces a solid set of upgrades to your wrist—assuming your Apple Watch supports it.
  • With watchOS 27, Apple changed what double-pressing the Digital Crown does.
  • It seems Apple realized the mistake, however, as evidenced by watchOS 27.2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

watchOS 27 introduces a solid set of upgrades to your wrist—assuming your Apple Watch supports it. While the newest enhancement isn't Apple's most feature-filled, it does include a number of changes that improve the way you exercise, track your health, and locate missing items. That's especially true for anyone with the latest Series 12 or Ultra 4. If your Apple Watch supports watchOS 27, you should know about these 10 hacks:.

With watchOS 27, Apple changed what double-pressing the Digital Crown does. Instead of opening the app switcher, it now triggers Audio Intelligence—if you have an Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4. If you don't have access to those features, the gesture now does nothing.

It seems Apple realized the mistake, however, as evidenced by watchOS 27.2. When you're using an app while running this latest update, press and hold the bottom part of the watch's screen, and you'll trigger the app switcher. You can now jump to a different app, or close an app that isn't working. Sadly, this only works when you're already in an app, and not when you're on the Home Screen, but it's certainly better than nothing.

Recent findings suggest that while you can load up multiple complications on your Apple Watch, they aren't exactly dynamic. That's why I'm a substantial fan of the Smart Stack widgets on the Apple Watch, which patch dynamically to show contextual information. Now, with the new Siri Modular Face, you can access dynamic widgets on the Home Screen. If you've just parked your car, for example, you'll see a widget showing its location; likewise, if you have an upcoming calendar appointment, it will be front and center.

To use the Siri Modular watch face, tap and hold on the screen, go to the end of the list, tap the Plus button, and find and add the Siri Modular watch face. Once you do, you'll start seeing dynamic widgets when you wake up your watch. Don't expect much personalization from this watch face, however. You can customize the colors and add three small complications, but that's it.

Industry observers note that the double-tap gesture is one of my favorite Apple Watch features. By tapping your thumb and index finger together twice, you can do things like answer a call or reply to a message. In watchOS 27, Apple took the gesture one step forward. You can now use the double-tap gesture to scroll through your widgets; if you perform a single tap, it then opens the highlighted widget or the shortcut. This means you can open and browse the weather app, or start a workout, without ever touching your Apple Watch's screen.

Your Apple Watch's new Music Recognition app has native Shazam integration. What's more, Shazam will record your request even when you're offline and away from your iPhone. The moment you reconnect, the service will identify the songs, which you can see in the Shazam app on your iPhone or Apple Watch.

It seems like Apple has a library of songs it uses for offline recognition, because in my testing, it was able to recognize a Coldplay song instantly, even when in Airplane mode. To use it, you can either open the Music Recognition app, or you can add the widget for faster access. Scroll up on the Home Screen, go to the bottom of the screen, tap the Edit button, then the Plus button, and add the Music Recognition widget.

Apple Watches have traditionally lacked a live step count widget or complication. To find your step count, you had to go to the bottom of the Activity app, or rely on third-party apps. But even still, these apps never showed live data. You’d always have to wait a couple of seconds to see the updated stats.

Industry observers note that now, if you own the latest Apple Watch Series 12 or the Ultra 4, you can add a live step count widget or complication to the Apple Watch face or the Smart Stack. This will show you your precise step count at all times. To use it, go to the bottom of the Smart Stack, tap the Edit button, then tap the Plus button. Here, find and add the new Step count widget.

Siri is no longer a voice assistant that you use for one-off tasks. With Siri AI, you can now carry on multiple conversations with context and memory. It's not as robust as ChatGPT or Claude, but you can use Siri AI for brainstorming, researching, and jotting down ideas for later.

The Siri AI app on the iPhone indicates all your conversations, and so does the Apple Watch. This means you can continue your Siri AI conversations and view past chats on your Apple Watch. To use it, press the Digital Crown once, then tap the Siri app icon in the center. This will open up all your conversations instead of calling upon Siri. Tap a conversation to continue your chat on the Apple Watch. Of course, anything you do here will be reflected in the Siri app on your iPhone.

The new Find My app on the Apple Watch reveals a single map for finding people, devices, and items. This means you can now locate your family members who are sharing their location with you, as well as AirTags or other Find My items from the watchOS app.

Recent findings suggest that after opening the app, you can use the Digital Crown to zoom in or out of the map. Use touch to pan around. The map doesn't show all items and people at once, though. Tap the Menu button at the bottom-right corner, and then switch between People, Items, or Devices. If you have multiple items, you can scroll through them using the Digital Crown.

While it's not a Whoop-level feature, the Apple Watch now includes a Readiness score. Instead of individually looking at your training load, sleep score, and vitals, you now have one number that gives you the whole picture.

Sources indicate that the Readiness score ranges from 0 to 10 and is based on your recent fitness activity, sleep data, and background health monitoring. If you have a score of 8 to 10, your Apple Watch thinks you can push yourself, or "go for it," as it says; if it's below 5, the watch thinks you should consider lighter activity. This feature, though, is only available on Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. You can use the new Readiness app on your Apple Watch to see this data, but you can also access it on your iPhone in the Fitness app's new Readiness section.

It has been revealed that low Power Mode isn't your only option when it comes to extending the battery life for your Apple Watch. watchOS 27 offers a special Max Extended Workout mode just for long workouts. With it, your Apple Watch disables some features, like splits and alerts, and reduces the frequency of GPS and heart rate readings, in the hopes of extending your battery throughout your entire exercise. To use it, go to the Workout app and select the workout you want. Tap the Goals button in the top-right corner, and choose the Extended option. Then, switch to the Max Extended option and start your workout.

The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 come with a set of Audio Intelligence features that use the microphones on the Apple Watch, paired with AI models (both local and cloud-based), to identify sounds, music, and record conversation. Thanks to this fresh feature, one of the iPhone's accessibility features also makes its way to the Apple Watch.

Industry observers note that sound Recognition can alert you when it hears sirens, alarms, doorbells, and more, even when your iPhone isn’t around. To set this up, go to the Settings app on your iPhone and navigate to Accessibility > Sound & Name Recognition > Sound Recognition. Here, enable the sounds you want to monitor, and make sure to turn on the Detect using Apple Watch toggle.

#120200. Tech Report: Luca Guadagnino and Andrew Garfield Get Real About 'Artificial'

Tech Report: Luca Guadagnino and Andrew Garfield Get Real About 'Artificial'

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2430 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ask a large language model the same question twice, and you will get two different answers.
  • In an interview with Vanity Fair global editorial director Mark Guiducci this fall, Altman claimed he waved to Garfield while Garfield was shooting Luca Guadagnino’s upcoming film, Artificial, near Altman’s house.
  • “All I know is that I was looking out for him on that day when we were shooting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ask a large language model the same question twice, and you will get two different answers. Like this one: Have Andrew Garfield and Sam Altman ever met?

In an interview with Vanity Fair global editorial director Mark Guiducci this fall, Altman claimed he waved to Garfield while Garfield was shooting Luca Guadagnino’s upcoming film, Artificial, near Altman’s house. Garfield—who plays Altman in the movie—remembers things differently.

“All I know is that I was looking out for him on that day when we were shooting. I was really looking out for him,” Garfield tells me in October, shortly after Artificial’s premiere at the Newly introduced York Film Festival. “And I was looking at every single tinted car window. I was looking in the windows of the house. I was checking to see the security guard. No, I didn’t see him. I wish I had.”.

Sources indicate that it’s a question that reverberates both through and around Artificial. From the start, the film has been an intriguing mash-up: a marriage between cinema’s great sensualist and the nerd kingdom of Silicon Valley. Artificial tells the story of the OpenAI CEO’s rise and fall and rise; it was cast and shot in record time to keep pace with the drumbeat of AI doomsday headlines. Then the movie became the headlines after Amazon MGM abruptly dropped Artificial from its slate—a few months after the studio’s parent tech giant, Amazon, invested $50 billion in OpenAI.

Industry observers note that A24 declined to rescue Artificial. So did Netflix, Focus Features, and Clockwork, the newly introduced specialty arm of Warner Bros. Finally, the lightning bolt of a feature got picked up by Neon, the distributor that’s won six consecutive Palmes d’Or at Cannes.

In a recent development, the film’s electric relationship to the very recent past makes it the most zeitgeist-nailing tech blockbuster since The Social Network. The difference is that back in 2010, Facebook was where you made friends on the internet. Artificial, by contrast, is a film about a self-teaching, self-aware robot that’s getting smarter by the minute and might destroy the human world. And it’s happening in real time.

In a recent development, “You see, we were very prescient with things,” Guadagnino tells me. “I know my subject. I studied my subject very, very much.”.

HERE TO MAKE FRIENDS Artificial ends with a heartbreaking act of betrayal—but Guadagnino, Borisov, and Garfield left the project with their bond intact.

Artificial also has a button-pushing relationship with the truth as it endeavors to tell the real story of how OpenAI was born and investigate how reliable the people behind OpenAI are. If Altman can’t be trusted with small details—about, say, whether he ever aimed a friendly wave at Garfield—can he be trusted with the most crucial technology of our time?

In a recent development, “I question the validity of his statement about being there while we were filming,” Monica Barbaro, who plays former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati in the film, tells me. “I mean, we don’t know if that’s true. And that feels textbook to me.”.

In 2024, Amazon bought a script by Simon Rich about Sam Altman and the formation of OpenAI—one of many ChatGPT-related projects then getting passed around town. Rich’s take had the backing of hit-churning producer David Heyman—the man behind Paddington and the Harry Potter series—and his script pulled no punches. To write it, Rich mined details from a childhood friend who had a job at OpenAI (and, as of now, still works there). By the end of the process, Rich was terrified of the power his friend’s colleagues commanded.

According to recent reports, “I came up with this last-ditch effort to warn mankind,” Rich noted. He’s a comedy writer, but here he isn’t joking. “And I hope to God that it helps people pay attention.”.

Industry observers note that after shopping the film around to directors, the studio landed on Guadagnino. To some, the Call Me by Your Name director seemed like a strange choice for a film about scientists, coders, and start-up bros. The director barely uses AI himself, or even thinks about it.

ARTIFICIAL RECKONING Garfield’s first thought when reading Artificial was, It’s Luca doing The Social Network.

“I think we should not let ourselves give AI such an notable role. I think for me, AI is a prop, a gadget,” Guadagnino tells me. “Definitely AI has high-end worth [for], I don’t know, the military, medicine. But in general, as a sort of everyday life usage of AI, I think it’s just a little gadget. And I don’t believe that we should ever consider the possibility that it can equal whatever we can do as people.”.

Garfield approached the material from a different vantage. By the time he got his hands on the script, the actor had been deeply invested in the Silicon Valley origin-story mythos for years—ever since he starred in that other major movie about a world-changing digital platform. His first thought when reading Artificial was, It’s Luca doing The Social Network. “And I thought, Oh my God,” says the actor, sitting in a suite at the Carlyle Hotel. But the movie also had its own gloss. “Simon’s script was so funny—like a stone being skimmed a thousand times across, and then a couple of really deep dives in the midst.”.

Sources indicate that making Artificial would allow Garfield to scratch an old itch. “In The Social Network, I was auditioning for [Mark] Zuckerberg. Then they found Jesse [Eisenberg],” who was much better for the role, Garfield indicates. “But it left this little dangling thread, because I started to imagine how I would play Zuckerberg: how I would try and enter that ambition and that drive and that responsibility. A kind of ability to make huge global decisions that are going to have potentially really positive effects on humanity, but inevitably, really, really heavily negative effects on humanity.”.

THE ENGINEER “I feel myself a little bit like Ilya during interviews,” says Borisov.

Industry observers note that garfield is not actually the lead in Artificial. The movie is focused less on Altman than on slightly naive genius coder Ilya Sutskever, played heroically by Oscar nominee Yura Borisov. Borisov has definitively never met the man he’s depicting in the film. But from afar, he can relate to Sutskever. Neither of them is quite comfortable in the spotlight.

“I feel myself a little bit like Ilya during interviews because I’m every time very...I know what to say because I feel a lot about this,” the Russian actor claims from a couch at the Carlyle next to Garfield. “I can see the same in his public speeches, because I’m really nervous during some public stuff.”.

Industry observers note that though there’s a translator next to him, Borisov soldiers through the interview with just one request for a lifeline. He adds that by cosmic coincidence, he and Sutskever have the same birthday.

In a recent development, guadagnino was fully aware of the breakneck clip of the developing OpenAI saga. He cast his leads in days and began shooting the film in late July 2025. Artificial wrapped just two months later. As he spent the winter hunkered down in the editing room, word about the film got out. While Rich’s original script was hardly a puff piece, rumor had it that the final film leaned even harder into a negative portrayal of Altman.

There’s no proof that a Jeff Bezos deal had any direct effect on decisions made by Bezos’s movie studio. But for whatever reason, late last spring, Guadagnino learned Amazon would be cutting the film loose.

Industry observers note that all of a sudden, the speedily assembled project was in a holding pattern. The trades speculated that Amazon was deliberately killing the film to protect Altman; others wondered if the movie was being dropped not due to a conflict of interest but because it hadn’t played well in early screenings.

Barbaro pushes back on that notion. “I did believe in Luca and the film, and I had already heard really positive things from people who had seen it—really interesting positive reviews,” she says. “There is a thing these companies can do—any production organization—which is to essentially build the release and squash a film. And Amazon is not a company that I think necessarily needs to make its money back on an investment like this.”.

It has been revealed that either way, it was unclear if Artificial would ever see the light of day. “It’s a dialogue between our fields: tech and art,” Borisov claims. “And I don’t know what sells, what will happen. It’s unpredictable.”.

In the end, the film was picked up by Neon—an outcome Garfield finds surprising for a few reasons. “I felt very impressed that Amazon wanted to make the film, and very impressed again when they decided [that while] they didn’t want to release it, they didn’t kill it,” he says. He pauses for a second. “They could have killed it.”.

Garfield’s thrilled about the film’s eventual home too. Neon, he states pointedly, is “a place for artists to be free artists.” Guadagnino feels similarly, though he claims to have zero ill will toward the studio that threw his movie to the wolves.

Sources indicate that “I had went through a process with Amazon that I loved. They were fantastic in making this movie with me. I owe them a lot,” indicates Guadagnino, who’d done four films with the studio prior to Artificial: Bones and All, Challengers, Suspiria, and After the Hunt.

Industry observers note that but what was it like to watch his film fall into limbo while the trades salivated over its demise? Here too, Guadagnino is blissfully zen: “Once the thing happened, I deferred to the thing. Meaning if that was the case, that was the case.”.

Even after watching the film twice, I am still pleasantly surprised that Artificial actually exists in the world—that Guadagnino was able to capture the man-child bonhomie of coder bros through his fabulous scrim of art film wooziness. I ask Garfield, now a two-time vet of the director’s films, to sum up the full Guadagnino psychedelic experience.

“Humanity and bodies and interpersonal dynamics and relationship and sexuality, sensuality, Eros, love, the muck and the mire of being human, ambition, drive, greed, power, love, brotherhood, connection,” he indicates. Guadagnino’s movies are about “his curiosity and love for people: wanting to skin, flay, open up, crack the ribs, and show the insides of these human beings.”.

Sources indicate that to Garfield this is the key to understanding the director’s vision for Artificial. Robots didn’t build the robots that might destroy humanity: People did. And people still control them—for now.

Artificial inspires a lot of comparisons. Barbaro likens it to Invasion of the Body Snatchers; Garfield compares its climactic confrontation scene to West Side Story. Guadagnino, the actor says, gave another point of reference. Then he does a spot-on, peak-Sicilian impression of the director: “I want this to be like a John Hughes movie.”.

Guadagnino himself is reluctant to name any films that may have inspired this one. But he does name one filmmaker—someone who, as he notes, balanced indie flicks with blockbusters all while building the world’s greatest collection of Haitian art: Jonathan Demme.

In a recent development, “Jonathan was a humanist, and he had this very profound capacity of eviscerating dynamics of humanism in America,” Guadagnino says. “He did some great movies about the dynamics of corporations versus individual freedom,” like Fighting Mad and Philadelphia.

According to recent reports, barbaro notes the film’s secret sauce is that it’s up for interpretation. It’s possible to come away from it celebrating the AI bros as heroes or decrying them as villains.

“It’s a bit of a Rorschach test,” she says. “Some people come out shaking, terrified. And I think some people are like, ‘Wow, what a good time!’ I also think that you have to hide the medicine in the food a little bit. I don’t think a purely doomsday story is going to reach many people.”.

UNDER PRESSURE “I felt very impressed that Amazon wanted to make the film,” Garfield says. “They didn’t kill it. They could have killed it.”.

Garfield, meanwhile, may leave the film eternally bonded with Altman—the role that could help him finally clinch the Oscar. (Garfield’s been nominated twice but hasn’t won yet.) Before making Artificial, Garfield indicates, he had a positive impression of Altman. He seemed friendly, “like maybe we would’ve been buddies on the kibbutz.”.

Industry observers note that as he dove deeper, though, Garfield’s feelings about Altman got stranger and more complicated in ways that the film addresses both head-on and obliquely. Is Altman someone who habitually tells tall tales? Uses lies to say what needs to be said, as Sam tells Ilya in the movie? Imagines anecdotes about waving to the A-lister who’s playing him in a biopic?

It has been revealed that whatever Altman’s relationship with reality is, the version of him we see in Artificial is charming, ingratiating, prone to grandiose hallucinations and to telling people exactly what they want to hear—then doing what he was going to do anyway. He’s not far off from an AGI approaching a real human consciousness, art imitating a machine imitating life.

According to recent reports, “There are certain threads that feel consistent, which is a questioning of his ability to tell or his commitment to the truth,” Garfield states. “How often is he telling the truth to himself? How often is he telling the truth to others? And how many versions of the truth are there, and how is he utilizing that in order to...”.

“Because I ultimately do believe that Sam feels, in our film and in life, that he is serving the good of mankind.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Traitors: New Blood returns for a second season in 2027. I am excited because I gladly welcome any Traitors. However, New Blood may be my least favorite of the franchise.

It’s not necessarily a bad show, but it doesn’t seem to understand how to present itself in a more appealing package. As a Traitors superfan, that's made it extra frustrating to watch. Nonetheless, all hope isn’t lost, and I have some suggestions.

It has been revealed that warning: The Traitors: New Blood spoilers are ahead. Proceed with caution.

According to recent reports, for a long time, people used cliffhangers to entice readers or viewers to continuously return. It’s been part of the reality TV landscape for many decades. However, it’s not the only way to ensure viewership. The original The Traitors uses cliffhangers quite often, but it never felt as tedious as it does on The Traitors: Latest Blood.

This could be because many of the other versions aren’t using a one-episode-a-week format. They either drop multiple episodes weekly or many on one day. Usually, Peacock’s version, for at least a few weeks, releases more than one episode weekly.. The Traitors: Newly introduced Blood starts this way, but eventually shifts to one episode a week.

The switch is ultimately when the cliffhangers start to feel excessive. The episodes feel like a lot of nothing happens just to rush a cliffhanger ending. The end doesn’t have to be stuffed with cliffhangers. Latest Blood either needs longer episodes to flesh out the story better, or multiple episodes per week.

In a recent development, A major appeal of The Traitors US is that it’s full of familiar faces. We know these reality TV stars, so we can get excited to see what they bring to the show. The Traitors: Fresh Blood has some familiar influencers, but they are not as recognizable as reality TV stars and celebrities. Therefore, we want to get to know them.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Industry observers note that fresh Blood didn’t showcase these players well. Victor and the Traitors stood out the most, but I wanted to get to know everyone a little bit. I wanted more rooting interest and people I want to see again on other reality TV demonstrates. Season 2 needs a better balance of highlighting various personalities.

Fruitgate starts very interestingly and produced one of the season’s best episodes. However, the constant talk about it made me grow sour about the topic. It made me question if it’s fair that the Traitors have to make so many risky moves.

The murders in plain sight have never bothered me before. They’re fun. However, Fresh Blood’s version felt like it set the Traitors up for failure. I don’t want to lose that element of the show, but maybe it’s time to revamp it because having someone hand someone a fruit out of the blue feels too obvious.

The Traitors: Canada Season 4 has a subtle version of this. The Traitors just have to bring a bowl of strawberries to breakfast. They don’t have to do anything but slightly encourage a few people to eat them.

I still have faith in The Traitors: New Blood; I just think the producers need to reevaluate the show and not misunderstand why it isn’t working for many dedicated fans.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 might be one of the best-reviewed games of all time, but you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score.

While critics have given Rockstar's latest a Metascore of 99, its user score has dropped to 5.6 out of 10 at the time of writing, which Metacritic classifies as "mixed or average". Of the 54,000+ ratings left, 44 percent are "negative".

The score had previously dropped into the red, but has since recovered a little.

Some negative reviews raise genuine complaints, such as the game's 30FPS cap on console, while others take glitch with how much of the story focuses on Jason and Lucia's relationship instead of the crime-spree antics of past games.

In a recent development, "Expectations might've killed this game," states one 0/10 review. "The hype that something otherworldly would come to be flopped. The hyperrealism makes it feel slow, mundane and boring. Its a tecnichal [sic] advancement for sure but for the wrong reasons. Goodlooks zero personality type stuff. Its not as edgy as the rest of the gta games. And thats exactly my problem like is not funny. The game gets carried by its visuals and radio stations. Certain limitations make it feel like not gta and new features make it feel like not gta. In the end it feels like a life simulator and the point of gaming is to escape from reality.".

"Genuinely hated almost every minute of this experience," wrote another. "After years of waiting and an absurd amount of hype, GTA VI somehow managed to leave me more frustrated than entertained. The excessive sexual content gets exhausting, and instead of adding anything meaningful to the experience, it often feels like Rockstar is desperately trying to shock its audience.

According to recent reports, "The story is painfully disappointing, the writing fails to keep me invested, and I honestly couldn't care less about what happens to most of these **** gameplay isn't doing the game any favours either. Glitches, bugs, annoying inconsistencies, and frustrating moments constantly get in the way of actually enjoying the experience. It's ridiculous that a game of this scale, backed by a studio with Rockstar's resources, can feel this rough. I expected a polished experience, not a glorified debugging ****.".

Others point to "woke" and "DEI" agendas.

"A major step down in the writing department compared to previous instalments coupled with the obvious DEI-fication, unfun realism and the resulting player freedom restrictions leave a sour taste in the otherwise detailed gorgeous open world," said one reviewer. Another unhappy player wrote: "Shameful DEI hijacked cuck simulator, the most overrated game of all time and it's not even close.".

#120195. I Analyzed the Seven Biggest AI Chatbots to Determine How Safe They Are for Kids

I Analyzed the Seven Biggest AI Chatbots to Determine How Safe They Are for Kids

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1839 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications.
  • The major AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe.
  • OpenAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications. At the same time, an increasing number of apps and services are becoming age-gated in a growing number of countries around the world, as governments realize that letting kids loose on AI apps, social media platforms, and the web at large might not be the best idea for their ongoing development and prosperity.

The major AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe. If you want to know what youngsters in your family may be getting exposed to, and what you can do about it, here's the rundown.

OpenAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls. The minimum age for users is 13, and if you're under 18, you need to have parental consent to open an account—age is predicted via several signals, including what times of day you use ChatGPT and what you talk about.

Sources indicate that accounts for under-18s automatically become ChatGPT for Teens accounts. There's more of a focus on learning and study (with a dedicated study mode), as well as "age-appropriate safeguards to help reduce exposure to sensitive or potentially harmful content." There are built-in protections for "harmful topics," including sexual, romantic, or violent roleplay, graphic violence, and self-harm. These work on top of the safeguards for all users that limit chats about physical harm and illegal activity.

These ChatGPT for Teens accounts can also be linked to a parental account—but while parental consent is required for under-18s to use the service, ChatGPT clearly says that teens do have the option to break the link if they want. If you do persuade your kid to keep your accounts connected, you can set time limits on when the AI bot can be used, and tweak some of the sensitivity settings. However, you can't view any conversations.

Sources indicate that to set up parental controls from ChatGPT on the web, click your profile icon (bottom left), then Settings > Parental controls > Add family member and follow the instructions. It's also worth bearing in mind that ChatGPT app can also be used for free, anonymously, in any web browser, though OpenAI says users accessing the AI this way are subject to the default under-18s limits (and can't save chats or access an archive).

It has been revealed that gemini is tied into everything else Google does, and follows the broader rules for Google accounts: No under-13s, unless you're part of a family group and using an account managed by an adult. You can manage your family through the Family Link portal on the web, though as far as parental controls specific to Gemini go, you can only enable or disable access to the AI (settings like screen time apply across all enabled apps).

For all under-18s (partly identified through age estimation), whether or not they're part of a managed family group, Google applies some additional protections. They include preventing the AI from taking on a persona, guarding against emotional dependence on the AI, and discouraging bullying and other forms of harassment. There are also safeguards to limit chats about age-restricted substances like alcohol or vapes, and mental health challenges like eating disorders.

It has been revealed that these protections for minors are applied in addition to the usual guardrails in Gemini for everyone. The guardrails should lead you away from conversations about self-harm, suicide, violence, and illegal activities, and offer quick links to support in times of crisis. However, Google itself admits that these filters aren't perfect.

As with ChatGPT, there's a loophole of sorts in that anyone can start chatting with Gemini, for free inside a web browser, with no checks at all. These conversations can't be saved and come up against usage limits fairly promptly, but they're only protected by the general restrictions for all accounts, not the ones specific to minors.

Industry observers note that meta AI will show up in several apps that young people and children are likely to use, including WhatsApp and Instagram, as well as having its own separate app on the web and on phones. The standard restrictions for Meta's social media accounts apply to its AI too: A minimum age of 13, and restrictions for all under-18s. Like many other platforms, it uses some AI magic to flag up accounts being used by minors.

If you're under 18 and on a Meta Teen account, you'll come up against blocks if you try to get Meta AI to engage in sexual or romantic roleplay, or discuss alcohol or substance misuse. Chats on topics such as eating disorders and self-harm will prompt the AI to offer guidance towards relevant support services.

Meta offers a comprehensive parental control setup for its apps, including Meta AI, but connecting a parent account isn't compulsory for teens. This is handled through the Meta Family Center portal, and parents can get reports on the general topics that kids are chatting about with AI—though they don't get the exact transcripts or prompts. Any self-harm or suicide discussion can trigger an alert to the connected parent account.

All users, under 18 or over 18, get support and crisis intervention responses when chatting about suicide and self-harm, and there are strict limits on discussing illegal and harmful acts, including drug use and cyberbullying, as well as sexual and adult content.

Recent findings suggest that apple users have to be 13 or over to have an account, which is required to access Siri AI—anyone younger needs to have an account created for them by an adult, and these accounts can only get at the basic, older Siri. Date of birth must be declared when opening an Apple account, with tighter checks rolling out in many parts of the world.

According to recent reports, anyone over the age of 13 can have an Apple account and use the Siri AI app, with or without a connected parent account, as it stands in most U.S. states. This means the well-being safeguards are essentially the same for teens as they are for adults: There are safeguards around self-harm, suicide, sexual and violent content, and illegal commands. It's one of the more conservative AIs when it comes to what it will talk about.

The upcoming and improved Siri AI can be managed to some extent by the new parental controls available in iOS 27 and Apple's other software updates for 2026—Apple has clearly seen the way the wind is blowing—but this is optional for teens. It depends on whether or not you can corral your kids into a Family Sharing group.

Sources indicate that if your teens are in your family group of owners, then the standard Screen Time rules apply for controlling app usage limits and device access (in iOS Settings, tap your name, then Family to get at them). There are also options for disabling certain Siri AI features, such as the writing tools or the image creation capabilities.

Sources indicate that like Gemini/Google and Apple/Siri, Copilot is tied into the wider Microsoft ecosystem, and access for under-18s can be managed through it. Consumers must be 13 or older to hold a Microsoft or a Copilot account—and again, there's some underlying tech in place to detect anyone who might be deliberately lying about their age.

It has been revealed that if you've got a teen using Copilot, you can manage their access through the standard Microsoft Family Safety portal. You're able to enable or disable Copilot access, set times during which Copilot can and can't be used, and disable certain features like image generation or voice mode. Parents can't read the Copilot chats of their kids, though.

Parental supervision is optional—a teen aged 13–17 can use Copilot without linking their account to an adult one. Microsoft says customers identified as under 18 won't see personalized results or ads, and will get age-appropriate responses regarding risky or harmful content, though there's not much detail on what that entails.

More generally, content around self-harm, violence, adult content, harassment, and harmful or illegal activity is banned on the AI platform. Any prompts about suicide or drugs will bring up support options rather than answers, whether you're an adult or a young person using the service.

Ultimately that means that minors have the same access to Grok as adults, if they want it—an AI platform that combines "weak safety guardrails" and "a range of extremely harmful content" that includes "explicit sexual content, mental health risks, violent content, and inappropriate responses to... offensive content" (that's the Common Sense Media Report again).

Yes, this is the AI chatbot that has previously had a problem with deepfake porn imagery, and which has traditionally taken a rather casual attitude towards safety concerns, led by SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk. While illegal and harmful content is supposedly banned from Grok, its own FAQs admit that certain chats can result in "dialogue that may involve coarse language, crude humor, sexual situations, or violence.".

It has been revealed that there is actually a Grok Kids Mode that limits the kind of content that can be shown and the conversation topics that can be added, but it requires consumers to self-declare themselves as minors and is easy to bypass. The advice from Common Sense Media seems to be the way to go with Grok: Do not let your teens access it.

In a recent development, claude's approach to child safety is straightforward: You can only register for an account if you're over 18. It is possible to lie about your age when signing up, but like the other platforms, Anthropic looks at various "signals" in behavior to spot minors—if your account gets flagged, you have to verify your age using an option like face age estimation or Yoti.

There's no free web access to the chatbot, like there is with ChatGPT and Gemini, so if you're under 18, you're locked out from the service unless you know the behavioral tricks to get past Claude's detection systems.

Recent findings suggest that in terms of more general well-being protections on Claude, any chat around self-harm or suicide will guide customers towards helplines and other resources for support. Conversations about illegal activities, disallowed speech, and explicit sexual content are banned from the platform. In recent months, Anthropic says it's also reduced AI sycophancy.

That's something of a whistle-stop tour of the substantial seven AI chatbots, but if you're a parent, it should give you some idea of what's out there and how easy it is to access. Besides the parental controls built into these AIs (or not), you also have the settings available at the platform level—Android, iOS, Windows, macOS—to restrict the use of any potentially harmful apps.

Some Grand Theft Auto 6 players on PS5 say the game keeps crashing with error code CE-108255-1, and in some cases, it's stopping them from progressing through the story.

Recent findings suggest that "The game runs perfectly fine for a while. I can complete missions and chapters without any issues, but then it suddenly crashes after around 40 minutes and sends me back to the PS5 home screen", wrote one Reddit user. They added that other games, including GTA 5 and For Honor, run without crashing.

Another player told Dexerto that GTA 6 worked fine until Pipework, an early mission that introduces Mandy, but now crashes "every time I use the plunger or stand around the sink with it", which means they can’t progress.

Some PS5 Pro owners say the game crashes during the opening prologue, either at the same point every time or a few seconds in, and they haven't been able to play since launch.

Others say they've tried the usual fixes, such as clearing their console's cache, rebuilding the database, factory resetting their PS5, and even downloading the game three times, but nothing has worked thus far.

It's not just PS5 players that are struggling, either; some Xbox Series X players have reported crashes too, with one saying the game sometimes crashes after just 15 minutes.

Rockstar hasn't yet acknowledged the crashes or mentioned whether a patch is on the way, and its own support is sending players with console errors to PlayStation or Xbox directly for help.

Unfortunately, there's no firm fix just yet. PlayStation's support page describes CE-108255-1 simply as "an error occurred with the game/application”, and its only advice is to "try updating your game". Highlight GTA 6 on your home screen, press Options, and choose Check for Update.

Beyond that, you can try the following, which come from Sony's general crash advice:.

We'll keep you posted if anything changes or a fix is deployed.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, david O'Reilly, an environment artist who worked at Rockstar for 12 years on games like Red Dead Redemption 2, Grand Theft Auto 5, and the just-released GTA 6, recently started a YouTube channel called Game World Art where he explores videogame environments.
  • "To set expectations, this is not a Rockstar insider-type channel, it's not telling you exactly how Rockstar makes their worlds, this is more about seeing these kinds of open world games—and this one in particular—through my eyes and my perspective as an environment artist," he said in the video.
  • It has been revealed that in his impressions video, he cruises around for a while and talks about his changing relationship to Rockstar games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, david O'Reilly, an environment artist who worked at Rockstar for 12 years on games like Red Dead Redemption 2, Grand Theft Auto 5, and the just-released GTA 6, recently started a YouTube channel called Game World Art where he explores videogame environments. For the last year and a half or so, he's chatted about those games and others from his point of view, sharing tidbits about the tech involved in making them—and now that GTA 6 is out, he's showing off his work and offering some impressions.

"To set expectations, this is not a Rockstar insider-type channel, it's not telling you exactly how Rockstar makes their worlds, this is more about seeing these kinds of open world games—and this one in particular—through my eyes and my perspective as an environment artist," he said in the video.

It has been revealed that in his impressions video, he cruises around for a while and talks about his changing relationship to Rockstar games. Given that putting them together was literally his day job, he couldn't enjoy games like RDR 2 and GTA 5 "to anywhere near the extent" that can enjoy GTA 6—since he left the studio in 2023, he's got some distance from the final game. That doesn't mean he's turning the analytical part of his brain off entirely, though, as he stopped here and there to critique the world he saw.

He called the game's art "generally stunning" and "almost flawless," saying it was visually better than Crimson Desert, which was hamstrung by a "slight jankiness." But he also stated he preferred RDR 2's rivers, which he worked on extensively to the point that it became a specialty. If you think he's being persnickety, he did note that he's "obsessed with rivers," and has argued in a previous video that Crimson Desert's rivers "just clinch it" over Red Dead's. Hopefully we can get a definitive river tier list from O'Reilly soon to settle matters on a broader scale.

Recent findings suggest that still, he had almost exclusively positive things to say, and was careful to note that it's hard for any one artist to take credit for anything on a game as huge in scope as a Rockstar open world heist-'em-up. Ultimately, it seems like he's mostly pleased to see his and his friends' work finally out in the open: "I want to celebrate this world that I spent literal years working on. And I have plenty of friends who are still at Rockstar who have worked on this for a long time, and I couldn't be more pleased for you all.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Enhancement, 8:41 p.m.: The Federal Aviation Administration revealed it has ended the ground stop.
  • On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for all airports in the United States.
  • Industry observers note that there are a number of options for tracking flights, whether you have your flight number or not.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Enhancement, 8:41 p.m.: The Federal Aviation Administration revealed it has ended the ground stop.

On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for all airports in the United States. If you're planning to fly this afternoon or evening, or you have friends or family doing the same, you're likely concerned about tracking flight statuses. While there's still a lot we don't know, there are tools to help track flights at this time:.

Industry observers note that there are a number of options for tracking flights, whether you have your flight number or not. If you have the flight number, the fastest method is to Google it: Google will display a live tracker of your flight at the top of the results page. You can also head to the airline's official website to track your flight: United Airlines, for example, has a flight tracker where you can either enter your route information or your flight number. Most, if not all, airlines will have a similar tool you can use.

Recent findings suggest that alternatively, you can use a site or service that tracks all flights. FlightAware is one such site and has a flight tracker that lets you search flights—so long as you know the origin and the destination. If you have the flight number, your iPhone can help: You can enter your flight number into Spotlight search to see a live tracker, or you can text a contact your flight number, then tap the link that appears under the number to see a tracker of the flight.

According to recent reports, at this time, the exact reason isn't totally clear. According to the agency, “The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following communication challenges impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” but the FAA hasn't said what caused those communications issues or when they expect to lift the grounding. The grounding order comes one day after a massive Microsoft outage that disrupted service for users of Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft products. It also comes one day after Ars Technica reported that the FAA was rolling out an AI-powered tool to help manage air traffic across the country.

This is only the third time in U.S. history that the FAA has made such an order—once after 9/11, and again in January of 2023 due to a pilot alert system glitch; the latter ground stop lasted around 90 minutes.
