Phasmophobia's next patch lets you ask ghosts to throw things and it's out next week

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (477 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Phasmophobia's next revision, Resonance, arrives on 24th November, bringing a brand-upcoming piece of ghost-hunting kit, more voice commands, and a move to the Unity 6 engine.
  • The headline addition is dowsing rods, which will help you track down the bone, making them particularly handy on bigger maps like Brownstone High School.
  • The Sound Sensor is getting an overhaul too, with a reworked interface to help you work out where sounds are coming from.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Phasmophobia's next revision, Resonance, arrives on 24th November, bringing a brand-upcoming piece of ghost-hunting kit, more voice commands, and a move to the Unity 6 engine.

The headline addition is dowsing rods, which will help you track down the bone, making them particularly handy on bigger maps like Brownstone High School. As with the rest of the game's equipment, the higher the Tier, the more accurate the reading, and Tier 3 Dowsing Rods will pinpoint the exact floor the Bone is on.

The Sound Sensor is getting an overhaul too, with a reworked interface to help you work out where sounds are coming from. Icons will show whether a sound is ongoing or a one-off, and you'll be able to use the map to identify ghosts by how fast they move.

You'll also be able to ask ghosts to interact with doors and switches, and even throw nearby objects, with a list of usable phrases in the Journal. If you're tired of the same maps, you'll be able to build your own pool of maps to randomise from when picking a contract, and new buttons let you promptly pick small, medium, or large maps.

"We want to ensure every item in our Ghost Hunters' kits can add as much value as possible in investigations," said Daniel Knight, CEO and game director at Kinetic Games.

"Resonance also brings Phasmophobia's move to Unity 6 - while this transition is a technical upgrade first and foremost, it has allowed us to implement major lighting improvements to make the game even more immersive.".

Alongside more realistic lighting and better stability, the switch to Unity 6 also brings expanded graphics and quality options, VR Eye Adaptation, and a suite of colour-blindness settings.

Resonance will also fix several prominent bugs, and introduce a conduct warning system that alerts players before they're banned, except in cases of severe violations.

Phasmophobia is also adding Xbox Play Anywhere support, so if you own the Xbox digital edition, you'll be able to play on Xbox Series X/S, PC, and devices like the ROG Ally.

Resonance is a free enhancement and will be available on all platforms.

Recent findings suggest that phasmophobia is available in Early Access on Steam, PS5, PS VR2, and Xbox Series X/S. It's also coming to Nintendo Switch 2, although we still don't quite know when.

Earlier this month, the Phasmophobia community raised more than $230,000 (around £173,000) for the American Heart Association, more than doubling last year's total.

Earlier this year, Kinetic Games confirmed Phasmophobia's 1.0 launch had slipped from this year into 2027, as the studio stated it was prioritising quality over speed following a rocky reception to its Player Character Revision. The studio ended up apologising to players for issues with the long-awaited update, admitting it "missed the mark" and "didn't deliver on our promises to you".

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that we've seen Glen Powell chase tornadoes, fly airplanes and play a football player in disguise. Next, he'll be transforming into a country singer for The Comeback King, a comedy he's collaborating with Judd Apatow on that will premiere on the 2027 movie schedule in February. So, what inspired him to put the cowboy hat back on and sing? Well, it turns out Twisters and shotgunning a beer with Luke Combs had something to do with it.

It’s not surprising to hear the Texas native is tapping into his country roots with The Comeback King, but I was surprised to find out the story would follow Powell as Aubrey King, a disgraced famous country singer who must revive his career, and that it was a comedy. After rave reviews for Season 2 of Powell’s Hulu comedy Chad Powers, I’m glad to see him stepping further into the comedic landscape after a string of action films like Top Gun: Maverick, Twisters, and The Running Man. However, I did not expect him to tell Katie and Organization that the inspiration behind this latest project stemmed from drinking beer with Luke Combs:.

I think it was when we were putting together Twisters. We were putting together the Twisters soundtrack that had, you know, Ella [Langley] and Megan Moroney, Bailey Zimmerman, Luke [Combs]. You know, it was like we had a great community, and I was like ‘Man, I just wanna be a part of this world.’ Probably right after I shotgunned beers with Luke Combs on stage. I was like, ‘I need to live here. I wanna do beers for breakfast just like Luke.’.

I can’t say I blame the Hit Man actor for getting caught up in that moment with his fellow Twisters castmates and Luke Combs. Together, they all shotgunned beer on stage at Combs’ NYC concert back in the summer of 2024, and the video went viral on TikTok.

As Powell mentions, he got a taste of the country music life putting together the Twisters movie soundtrack, which hit no. 3 on the Billboard country album charts that summer, with Luke Combs’ “Ain’t No Love In Oklahoma” spending 15 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100.

According to recent reports, A tale as old as Rocky, if you want a part in a specific film, write it yourself. According to Rolling Stone, Producer Kevin Misher connected Powell with Apatow shortly after the idea for The Comeback King was born, and the Scream Queens actor and the mind behind Knocked Up wrote the script together. This will be Apatow’s first directorial feature film since The Bubble (2022) and The King of Staten Island (2020).

I’m already sold on The Comeback King from the trailer alone. It’s got hilarious roasts, a redemption arc, and a ton of heart, all the hallmarks of a great Judd Apatow film. In The Comeback King, we see Glen Powell live out his wildest “beer for breakfast” fantasies (a nod to Luke Combs “Don’t Tempt Me”), until it all comes crashing down after his pop star girlfriend (Madelyn Cline) cheats and ruins his reputation. King then returns to his old college where his career all started, for redemption and maybe a new shot at love. Check out the trailer below, and see if you can name the insane number of country music cameos:.

Industry observers note that how Glen Powell was able to once again assemble the Avengers of country music, I’ll never know. But I’m super excited to see the likes of Miranda Lambert, Jelly Roll, Brad Paisley, and Shaboozey bring their A-game alongside Powell in this epic ensemble comedy when it premieres on February 5, 2027. While we wait for that, I think we should all say thank you to Luke Combs too for helping inspire this film that looks like it'll be a lot of country fun.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A rating for the unannounced Nioh 3 Complete Edition has popped up on Korea's Game Rating and Administration Committee (GRAC).

As Insider Gaming spotted, the board gave Nioh 3 Complete Edition a 19+ rating on 17th November after it was submitted on 2nd November, even though Koei Tecmo hasn't declared a Complete Edition for the game yet.

The listing, translated by machine, describes it as "a compilation of additional content from the dark Sengoku action RPG Nioh 3", and gives the rating for "excessive expression of violence", noting that "red blood and body amputation frequently occur during combat".

The listing also notes an overseas rating, which Insider Gaming says is a 17+ rating from Japan's CERO.

Unlike some rating boards, GRAC publishes its ratings as soon as they're decided, which is why game listings often surface there before they're officially unveiled.

Recent findings suggest that if Koei Tecmo follows the same pattern as Nioh 2, there may not be long to wait. GRAC's records show Nioh 2 was rated in January 2020, and its Complete Edition followed in November that year. Nioh 3 was rated on 14th November 2025, almost exactly a year ago.

Complete Editions typically includes the base game and all of its DLC. It could even launch alongside Nioh 3's second DLC, Bloody Insurrection, which is due in February 2027. Eurogamer has contacted Koei Tecmo for comment and we'll let you know if/when they come back to us.

Back in April, an update introduced "multiple high-difficulty Battle Scrolls" (side missions), accessible from shrines, the addition of a Stone of Penance item "which increases accessory +Values and rarities in exchange for higher difficulties", and new skills given as rewards for completing the aforementioned high-level Battle Scroll missions.

Eurogamer's review of Nioh 3 called the threequel a new high for the 'masocore' series and "the crucible in which all of Team Ninja's experience has been siphoned into." It's sold over one million copies (and counting) since its 6th February launch.

I’m seeing reports that some folks have already blazed through GTA 6‘s story, finishing the game roughly 48-ish hours (depending on your time zone) after its release. And of course, there are those gamers who don’t plan on playing the game at all, untouched by the powerfully seductive force of GTA 6 FOMO. Whatever your reason for having a free gaming calendar right now, I’ve come bearing gifts with which you can fill it. I’ve sampled my Kotaku colleagues as well as conducted my own research to assemble a smattering of recently released indie games you can play right now.

Recent findings suggest that dig Dig Dino was originally released on the Playdate before coming to Steam this week. It’s from the developers of the well-liked western action game Arco, though this time they’ve gone for something much smaller, simpler, and cuter. In Dig Dig Dino you play as an paleontology intern tasked with using your shovel and a growing arsenal of tools to find dinosaur bones. You start with limited stamina, only able to dig so much in a day. But as you chew through layers of dirt and sedimentary rock, you pick up treasure that gets exchanged for cash with which you can buy more more stamina, upgrades for your tools, and latest tools like a dog who will sniff out bones for you.

Industry observers note that the game sounds almost too simplistic to be any kind of fun, but I found myself spending hours digging, hoping the next run would reveal the final piece to my saurian puzzle. There are different dig sites that require different tools and yield different treasures, but don’t expect to discover the kinds of finds that would excite the dearly departed Dr. Alan Grant. The dinos you discover in this game are weird, and though I’m only a few hours (and a few competed skeletons) in, I suspect there’s a greater mystery about the world to discover as you dig deeper.

Sources indicate that sonic Pico Park may have the blue blur in the name, but itâs developed by the small team at TECOPARK, which created the original Pico Park. The cooperative puzzler lends some Sonic the Hedgehog flair toÂ Pico Park‘s cooperative, ragebait puzzle platforming action. The game is a lot of chaotic fun in which up to eight players will yell at one another, then lock in to solve some difficult challenges. Work on your team-building skills as Sonic, Shadow, and several other characters from across the series. Lone wolves need not apply; youâve gotta play with folks you can still like after youâve been tied to one another and tried to coordinate running through a loop-de-loop. â Kenneth Shepard.

It has been revealed that maybe you’re a big fan of Dark Souls, Elden Ring, or even King’s Field. Maybe you’re craving that next Elder Scrolls. Or maybe you’re just not super interested in cars and guns and want something a bit more medieval. Friends, let’s pay a visit to Queen’s Domain, a gorgeous first-person RPG in classic-PlayStation style that combines a very clonky, retro-feeling combat and exploration system with much more smoothness to movement and menuing than the games that inspired it could ever muster. Queen’s Domain has you exploring a mysterious island full of magic and monsters in search of your father. You’re puny and weak when you start, enemies hit hard and sneak up on you, and for the most part the game tells you very little about how to proceed: you just have to experiment and pray. But that’s exactly what some people (like me) want, and the feeling when something finally clicks is exhilirating. I hear there’s a pretty big twist midway through that blows the game wide open, too, though I haven’t experienced it yet for myself. â Rebekah Valentine.

Sources indicate that tanuki: Ponâs Summer is one part Tony Hawk, one part mail delivery game, and one part cozy slice-of-life sim. Also, you play as an adorable Tanuki who waddles around the open-world village and forest that make up the game’s map. Iâve had a lot of fun pulling off sick tricks while delivering packages to locals and learning more about them. Sometimes, these moments lead to mini-games in which you help out the villagers with sumo wrestling, running a bar, or chopping down trees. But mostly, you spend a lot of time doing tricks on a BMX bike in a gorgeous little world that Iâve been having a great time poking at between big GTA 6 sessions. â Zack Zwiezen.

Wanderburg is a bullet heaven action-roguelike in which you play as a medieval fortress on wheels swerving around the countryside as armies collide and new territories are conquered. Itâs sort of like Vampire Survivors if it starred the castle from Howlâs Moving Castle. Itâs also similar to TerraTech Legion, another vehicular spin on the auto-shooter genre, except with some Age of Empires flavor mixed in. Itâs in Early Access on Steam right now and itâs my go-to run-based arcade shooter for the fall. – Ethan Gach.

CRACK is a type of game that’s not usually my bag. Itâs an incremental co-op comedy adventure, not something Iâd usually touch, but my son loves these types of games and so I spent more time with it than I expected to. You live in a mysterious lab with a giant egg in the middle. Your job is to crack pieces of it off and trade them in for money, which you use to get upgrades to get better tools to knock off better chunks of the egg and, well, you can see where this is going. But the egg is alive, and the more you chip away the angrier it gets, eventually causing dangerous outbursts that lead to chaotic mayhem. Thatâs the friendslop part of it. Throw in the mystery of the lab itself, with clear influences from games like Portal, and youâve got a surprisingly clever social twist on making the numbers go up. – Ethan Gach.

Well Dweller is the fourth metroidvania by Kyle Thompson, and if you donât know who that is, just think Hollow Knight but shorter and more chill. While seemingly influenced by Team Cherryâs aesthetic sensibility and gameplay formula, Thompson has been refining his own take on the genre for several games now. Plus you know what? Silksong came out over a year ago. We could use a spiritual successor or two, and Well Dweller earns its keep as one of the better ones. You play as a bird with a matchstick that can do all sorts of whimsical things, leading to some satisfying traversal and combat, even if itâs not very deep. For those who want a breezier action metroidvania, thatâs a plus. – Ethan Gach.

Sources indicate that have you heard the good word of Dressmaker yet? Dressmaker is about exactly what you think it is: you make dresses. But itâs not just a color-swapping dress-up game. No, youâre doing this stitch-by-stitch. Youâre choosing the fabric, picking out adornments, cutting pieces to patterns along the bias, stitching them together, adding the lace trim, all to customer (or your own) specifications. The ridiculous amount of detail that Dressmaker goes into, coupled with an enormous array of dressmaking options that you unlock as you play, already has made it a beloved favorite this year. And some of the dresses people are making are ridiculous! But whether youâre skilled or just throwing together some cloth, Dressmaker is undeniably delightful. – Rebekah Valentine.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that welcome to Disk Cleanup, our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a newly introduced interview, digging into the notable questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?".

Playing on school computers has been a rite of passage for many young PC gamers, whether through dedicated edutainment titles or rogue installations by chancing pupils. But fantasy novelist Scott Lynch went one step further: he took the school computers home.

In a recent development, "My mother worked for our school district, so I'd occasionally have the chance to sneak into the computer lab, or we would borrow and Apple II over the summer," Lynch states. "When we did that, I borrowed Infocom games … text-only adventure games from the '80s like Zork, Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Planetfall, A Mind Forever voyaging. I was really into those when I was about 12.".

Text-based adventures would eventually become a defining feature of Lynch's life, albeit in a different format. His debut novel, The Lies of Locke Lamora, was published in 2006, charting the schemes and adventures of a group of master con artists called The Gentleman Bastards. Two further novels in The Gentleman Bastard Sequence have since followed: 2007's Red Seas Under Red Skies, and 2013's The Republic of Thieves.

Industry observers note that lynch presently working on a novella in the same world called More Than Fools Fill Graves, as well as his highly anticipated fourth novel, The Thorn of Emberlain. "It is something that I am absolutely working on and trying to be as open and honest about as possible," he notes. But he took a quick break from writing elaborate fantasy heists to show me around the treasure-filled vault of his Steam library.

I have reopened Morrowind for the first time in a number of years. Right around the time I was working on my first novel and had not finished it yet, I was playing it on the original Xbox. Other than the fact I was like 23, 24, I can't fathom how I did that.

I've been meaning to go back to Morrowind for ages, but I was put off by the jankiness of the UI, the quality-of-life experience, or the thought that there were just enough rough edges of this game that's now nearly a quarter of a century old, that I wouldn't enjoy it.

I was talking to another author who maybe has a bad computer game habit, and he turned me on to OpenMW. He posted some screenshots on Bluesky of some beautiful-looking Morrowind vistas and some nice skies and vegetation. And I thought "A-ha! Here's a man that uses mods." So even though I own a copy of Morrowind, like the fourth copy I've bought in my life, I'm now using OpenMW, and I'm loving it.

From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews.

The thing that I enjoy about Morrowind is the incredible granularity of its various subsystems and the game-breaking things that you can do with processes like alchemy and enchantment. And the fact you can enchant layers of clothing and be wearing enchanted underwear underneath your enchanted armour. [But] I set a bunch of rules for my character, because usually I play something along the lines of a wizard who can go anywhere, do anything, build high-powered potions to fly all over the landscape at high speed.

I decided that I would play something along the template of a Paladin, and I gave myself a very limited powerset that I could create utilising the custom spell-builders … so I have a very limited toolset, and I opted to spend more time actually wandering around the world doing quests, and less time sitting in one place making 10,000 potions.

I played Skyrim to death [with] many character concepts, and one of my favourites was a little ruleset that I called the Conan playthrough, where you play as melee-type character who cannot use magic at all … you place all these rules and limitations upon yourself. What I found is that narrowing the focus of the game experience can be as liberating as having a completely open world before you, and I've rediscovered that with this particular Morrowind playthrough.

It's a game from the late '90s called Star Wars: Rebellion, which over in the UK would have been known as Star Wars: Supremacy. It's elderly, it's janky, its UI and its quality of life are from a previous era of human development. It's absolutely full of problems. But it's also got kernels of brilliance, and there's never been anything like it ever since. As a Star Wars fan, I find myself returning to it over and over, as a dog to his vomit.

Sources indicate that I've still got Master of Orion 2, and it's still playable, which is from '90s. I love MOO2. I've played it to death in every possible permutation. I last played Master of Orion about five years ago. That would have also been in the pandemic.

You can see how nearly every game in the 4X space has been trying for the last three decades to, in some fashion, be that game and recreate its experience, and that's a very difficult thing to do … MOO2 just has a certain smoothness to it.

I've tried to get into other 4X games … but I just don't think that any 4X space game since MOO2 has successfully emulated that smoothness of pickup and that open sense of play, as in "Where's my civilization going to go?".

Recent findings suggest that to a certain extent when you play a game like MOO2, outside the bounds of creating a custom species and a custom culture, you're playing with somebody else's IP, and when I play a game like that, I look for a certain degree of possessiveness, a certain degree of personalisation. I want to play my species' story and I don't necessarily want to play with somebody else's narrative IP.

All right, let's look at the embarrassing total. All I'm going to say about this is that if J.R.R Tolkien had had a Steam account, his numbers would be pretty embarrassing too.

I've got a couple of suspects. Star Wars: Rebellion, keeping in mind, this is since 2012, because that's when I noticed that it was on Steam and I went 'Oh, cool.' At 1,493 hours. That'll be hard to top. Fallout: Newly introduced Vegas, only 630 hours, but that's also a bit of a lie because I had that game on two different Xbox 360s.

But the winner is definitely BattleTech. I've got a truly embarrassing 1,564 hours. I spent a lot of time commanding a BattleTech company during the pandemic.

It has been revealed that I have played this so much. I have experienced every bark, every random event, every edge and corner, I have played it to a point beyond which it was designed to be played … After you've played a game for 1,500 hours, you see problems that would not be visible to a normal human being.

I have experienced every bark, every random event, every edge and corner.

Sources indicate that it is janky. It is imperfect. It is a notorious memory leak rat bastard that can hang and slow down forever. But it is a marvellous, diverting game that does exactly what it promised, designed by people who really love the setting and really love the playstyle, with just marvellous production design. It really returns that feel of being 12 or 13, poring over old BattleTech manuals and wishing I had somebody to play the game with who was as obsessive as me.

Industry observers note that the whole '80s, early '90s mecha genre has always been a huge fascination for me. When I was 12 or 13, I saw [BattleTech]. I'm in a gaming store and I see this game that has the Robotech Mecha … I could not resist it. I've just retained a love of that. It's not a deep philosophical thing. One just loves to see giant robots slugging the hell out of each other with lasers and so forth.

The fun thing about BattleTech as a setting, and I'll put my writer hat on for a moment and attempt to recover some of my street cred—"What are your influences? Oh, Dostoevsky, Atwood, BattleTech." BattleTech's secret weapon is that it is a game universe that is full of holes and mysteries. It's a period of ongoing civil war after the collapse of the Star League, the great hegemony across the known galaxy, and so that means there are vanished cultures, vanished planets, vanished fleets, just entire holes in the column of historical knowledge where all sorts of things can be hiding.

So some of the fun of the BattleTech lore is that it's not for perfecting. It's not for memorising. It is inherently a big dark mystery that fills the entire galaxy.

Oh God, I am going to play Star Wars: Rebellion until the heat death of the universe. I've just accepted that now. I'm never going to uninstall Fallout: Latest Vegas for as long as it's allowed.

Industry observers note that there was something else …. OK, Knights of the Old Republic. I'm not sure I will ever play it again, but it's a game I am deeply attached to because it is superbly written, beautiful production values, loads of fun, and a very good adaptation of the then-current Star Wars tabletop system.

It came along just at the right time, because this was right after Attack of the Clones. I am a lifelong Star Wars fan. The original three movies might as well be tattooed on the back of my eyelids. But there was a time around 2001, 2002 when that love really needed some buttressing.

In a recent development, all of a sudden, here comes Knights of the Old Republic, which is the full package. Sweeping emotion, great story, wonderful characters, full of details, beautiful soundtrack. It just restored that sense of 'OK, I know why I'm a Star Wars fan'.

If forced to remove that from my library, I would do it with trembling hands.

Recent findings suggest that there's a [program] called WriteRoom, and it's a screen distraction destroyer. It just blots out and covers up everything else on your screen and gives you nothing but a blank white space, or a blank configurable space depending on your preferred background and text colour. It's just a blank white screen with a cursor on which you write.

It has been revealed that it's a focus tool. I don't use it every day, but there are days when I do need to use it to recover my train of thought and say, "This is the world, this is where my entire brain goes." It provides a cosmetic trick that blots everything else out. I'm sure there are other apps of this nature, but that's the one I've used.

I do clean it up well enough that it's not absolute horror. However, it's not as good as it could be. I want to say that it is just on the wrong side of optimised. 15% too cluttered.

Every couple of days, I'll delete four things and pat myself on the back and say, "Look what I did!" And then the next day, I'll add five things.

Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex. Between 2013 and 2022, Rick was games editor of Custom PC magazine and associated website bit-tech.net. But he's always kept one foot in freelance games journalism, writing for publications like Edge, Eurogamer, the Guardian and, naturally, PC Gamer. While he'll play anything that can be controlled with a keyboard and mouse, he has a particular passion for first-person shooters and immersive sims.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SPOILERS ahead for Percy Jackson and the Olympians' Season 3 two-episode premiere, now streaming for those with a Disney+ subscription or Hulu subscription.

Industry observers note that did anyone else watch Percy Jackson Season 3 and think about how much our demigods have grown up? Somehow, we’ll be halfway through Rick Riordan’s original five-book series on the 2026 TV schedule literally next week! However, as book readers know, the closer we get to The Last Olympian, the closer we are to Percy and Annabeth finally being an item, and I, for one, can’t wait. And, in the first two episodes alone, I already feel the chemistry between these two elevating.

It has been revealed that the last time CinemaBlend caught up with the showrunners, they told us they’re trying to “slow burn” the relationship between Percy and Annabeth. When I caught up with them again, Jonathan E. Steinberg delved into where we’re at this season with their dynamic, saying this:.

I think it's key, period. I think that story is their story in every way that's meaningful as the spine of this series. I think the challenge this season is they’re not in the same place. And, I think that puts a lot of pressure on the moments in which they are to be making those moments meaningful. And, I think it puts a lot of pressure on what it puts them through to be separated from each other and what they would do to make sure the other's OK, and how much you feel that.

It has been revealed that oh, I feel it. I mean, what sticks out to me so far is that dance scene between them in Episode 1. After Percy famously told Annabeth he would “burn it all down” for her last season if he had to, you can feel this unsaid chemistry between them. However, in true teenage boy fashion, Percy shoots down the comment when Annabeth brings it up. Then, right before she gets captured by the manticore, Percy looks like he was about to risk everything to try to save her if Artemis didn’t pull him off the ledge.

And, as someone who's seen the next two episodes (but I promise I won’t tell), there’s even more where that came from. Steinberg also remarked this during our recent chat:.

So, I think it does its job as the middle chapter of the book series and kind of where we are in the bigger story. I think by the time you get to the end of the season, you feel it. If you are somebody who read these books and knows where this is going and knows where it ends, the show is not just tracking that, but it's adding really meaningful depth to what that moment will mean eventually, and to what they mean to each other in the moment now.

According to recent reports, season 3 really feels like the sweet spot for Percy and the rest of the cast, where they are at the right age for the show to mature a bit more, and that makes me more excited for what’s to come. I know there’s always discourse around the book changes in TV shows like this, but I like what’s been done so far. For one, we’re getting to see Annabeth’s time in captivity, and we’re also getting more Percabeth moments ahead of the pair going from friends to romantic partners.

In a recent development, there’s so much more to get excited for regarding the adaptation of The Titan’s Curse! Two fresh episodes will drop on Disney+ and Hulu every Friday until finale week on December 11.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Grand Theft Auto 6 player says they've been hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network social features ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

Posting on Twitter/X on Friday evening, DerrickGott007 remarked they had "just got a 30-day PSN social features ban" for sending the photo, which they'd taken with the in-game camera, through PlayStation's messaging service, warning other players not to do the same.

Sources indicate that "Do not, I repeat do not send any photos taken with the in-game camera, across the PSN messaging network that contain nudity," they wrote. "I just got a 30-day PSN social features ban for sending my friend a photo of the nudist colony in GTA6 that I found.".

It has been revealed that in a screenshot of the notice, PlayStation Safety states that content sent from the player's account via Message on PlayStation "breached the Code of Conduct", and that their account has been "temporarily suspended from using PlayStation social features for 30 days" due to "pornographic or obscene content". It also warns that "further offenses may result in temporary or permanent suspension from the whole of PlayStation, not just social features".

PlayStation's Code of Conduct asks players not to "share, solicit, access, distribute or store material that is obscene, pornographic or illegal", and says Sony "may take any action as reasonably necessary to protect PlayStation and our players".

Industry observers note that DO NOT, I REPEAT DO NOT SEND ANY PHOTOS TAKEN WITH THE IN GAME CAMERA , ACROSS THE PSN MESSAGING NETWORK THAT CONTAIN NUDITY. I JUST GOT A 30 DAY PSN SOCIAL FEATURES BAN FOR SENDING MY FRIEND A PHOTO OF THE NUDIST COLONY IN GTA6 THAT I FOUND. pic.twitter.com/vsoIjmpGrt.

Recent findings suggest that crucially, as Dexerto points out, the code does not make an exception for content taken from games, even ones rated for adults. So if you've snapped anything cheeky in Leonida - say, full-frontal nudity in its nudist resort - you might want to keep it to yourself.

GTA 6 released on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's one of the best-reviewed games of all time, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Industry observers note that eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. How To Solve All Main Puzzles In GTA 6′s Tenebrae Lux

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, if you decide you’d rather sit at home all day and play a pretentious, cerebral puzzle game instead of go on heists, Tenebrae Lux is waiting for Jason and Lucia on their JoyStation in GTA VI.
  • But I’m assuming you’re here because you either want to beat it quickly, or you’ve gotten so stuck (as I did) on a few of the puzzles that you’re desperate for help.
  • You can’t do much: just walk around and examine objects.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6Grand Theft Auto VI.

According to recent reports, if you decide you’d rather sit at home all day and play a pretentious, cerebral puzzle game instead of go on heists, Tenebrae Lux is waiting for Jason and Lucia on their JoyStation in GTA VI. While on the surface it looks like just a funny gag poking at auteur culture (and one developer in particular), Tenebrae Lux is a surprisingly solid, short puzzle game that (if you’re not using this guide) may take you a few hours to get through.

But I’m assuming you’re here because you either want to beat it quickly, or you’ve gotten so stuck (as I did) on a few of the puzzles that you’re desperate for help. I get you. Here’s as simple a walkthrough as I could manage for Tenebrae Lux:.

You’ll start out on the shoreline. You can’t do much: just walk around and examine objects. To start with, you’re going to want to head to the left side of the shore (assuming you’re facing the shore from the beach you start on) where there are multiple run-down shacks lit by substantial bright lights.

Sources indicate that inside these shacks are three puzzles on gridded boards. On those grids, multiple pieces are placed with different 3D shapes atop: three-tiered tall ones, middling spiky ones, and flat ones with a tiny dot in the middle. The flat ones don’t move at all, the middle-sized spiky ones can slide across the board and clear the flat ones if they land next to them, and the three-tiered tall ones and middle-sized ones clear one another in the same fashion. Your goal is to clear all the pieces off the board.

Recent findings suggest that you can do these puzzles in any order. One of them is easy and straightforward, but the other two require a little bit more thinking. You’ll have to use the fact that the flat pieces don’t move and cannot be cleared by the three-tiered pieces to set up the three-tiers so they and the mountain pieces can clear one another once all the flat ones are off the board.

Recent findings suggest that the three main puzzles in this area should be fairly simple to do, though there are a couple of hidden ones you can optionally do that are more difficult. On at least one, you might need to set up your board so you have two three-tier pieces set up with a gap between them that a middle-sized piece can easily get into after clearing a flat one. See below:.

When I move that mountain-shaped piece to the left, it will take out itself and all three of those other tiles with it.

This puzzle will easily make you feel like you’re losing your mind, but I highly recommend trying to work it out for yourself first, if you can.

When you enter the room upstairs in the bunker, you enter a loop that will keep perpetuating each time you go through the door and up the stairs. The room will be almost identical each time you enter it, but for two things. The first will be the calendar, which will show the date as being one of six different dates, and the second will be one of the other objects in the room.

Your goal is to find a six-digit code and enter it into the phone, followed by the # sign, to proceed.

It has been revealed that in order to get the code, you need to pay attention to what day it is, and what is different in the room on that date. If you keep going up the stairs over and over, the dates will eventually cycle back through, so if you miss one don’t worry, you can keep going to see it again. The dates are as follows: October 11, 14, 20, 23, 27, and 30. You won’t see the dates in any particular order, but you’ll need to put them in that order when you input the numbers for each date into the phone.

Recent findings suggest that the numbers themselves, you get from finding what’s “different” in the room on a given date, and working out what number the difference corresponds to. There are ten possible differences, and your playthrough won’t have all these objects in the roomâit’s random each time, though consistent within a single playthrough of the puzzle. Here are the ten possible differences:.

Once you get the code right, exit upwards one last time and on you go.

This one was waaaaay more confusing to me than it needed to be. The goal is to cross the bridge off to the left of the ruins. The bridge has multiple rows of weird symbols on it. You have to walk over the correct symbol in order to proceed. If you walk over the wrong one, a lamp will go out. If you do it wrong three times, you fail and the puzzle resets.

The trick to figuring out the correct symbols is in the ruins and the poem on the plaque just outside.

The ruins will contain the following items, which correspond to the following descriptors in each of the seven lines of the poem:.

It has been revealed that the items will be scattered across the ruins. Also in the ruins you will find a bunch of weird, esoteric symbols glowing on the ruined archways above. These symbols correspond to the symbols on the bridge.

To solve this, you need to visit each of the items in the order they appear in the poem, and match the item with the symbol on the ruins that corresponds to it, then follow the symbols across the bridge in order (the direction they’re facing doesn’t matter). It can be a bit tricky to figure out which symbol goes with which item. The best way I can describe it is the symbol for each item is the one that’s over the doorway “entrance” to each item, so the one you have to pass under to reach it.

Here’s a map to show you what I mean. Orange circles are places where the objects can appear, and green triangles are where symbols are. I’ve numbered them, but please don’t mistake the numbers for the correctÂ order of the objects: that’s going to be determined by the poem, and the poem’s order is random.

Also note that #1 below is on the ground, because the arch has collapsed.

This can still be confusing, so let me walk you through what I got as an example. Here’s my poem:.

First up is moon, which for me was straight ahead through the first door.

It has been revealed that two days of rest says nothing, so we move to the third line, which mentions forests. Here’s the tree:.

Sources indicate that third verse mentions gold, then earth, in order. My trophy was past the mark that had crumbled to the ground, and my earth was at the very start of the puzzle:.

Recent findings suggest that this next line is a bit tricky, as it mentions both sun and moon. But there are only seven lines on the bridge, and the items are only used one time each. So we just focus on sun here. I didn’t get a good picture of my sundial, sorry!

It has been revealed that the last two lines in order mentions fire first, then drinking, which is water. Here’s fire:.

Sources indicate that so I’d follow those symbols in order across the bridge. It may help to draw a map on a piece of scrap paper or in a notebook for this one so you don’t have to slowly walk back and forth over and over.

If you fail, the puzzle will fully reset itself, and you’ll have to look at a new version of the poem and ruins and try again.

It has been revealed that this bit is a little creepy and again confusing at first, but quite easy once you work it out. All you have to do is walk in the door that’s the furthest away from any of the figures walking through the doors.

In the photo above, the man is walking toward the third door from the right, so I want to go to the farthest door on the left.

As you go, more figures will start to appear. When there are multiple, you want to try and split the distance as best as possible. You also have to avoid any doors that say they’re out of order, so if they have a sign on them, go to the next one furthest away from the man. On the last set of doors, there was no way to get away from the men, so I just walked directly between two of them.

Once you pass through the last door, you’ve officially beaten Tenebrae Lux!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Many people know of my mama, Avie Lee Owens Parton, from my song “Coat of Many Colors,” but my mama gave me a gift that was far more valuable than a colorful coat. She gave me the gift of music.

Avie Lee, Dolly, and Robert Lee Parton.

Recent findings suggest that as far back as I can remember, Mama loved to sing—at church, at family get-togethers, and most of all to her children. Her love of music came naturally; she had inherited it from her parents, her grandparents, and all the way back to Wales, where her family, the Owens, came from. Most of all, she inherited her love of music from her father, the Rev. Jake Owens. Grandpa Owens was a singer, songwriter, musician, and music teacher, in addition to being a full time Pentecostal preacher. He and my grandma Rena raised eight children, and all of them took to music in one way or another.

So, it was a natural thing that Mama shared her love of music with her children. She especially loved the old mountain songs—ballads that reached all the way back to the British Isles, popular songs from the 1800s that mountain people had made their own and, of course, beloved hymns.

Recent findings suggest that so, when my uncle Louis Owens, Porter Wagoner, and I opened Fireside Recording Studio in Nashville in 1973, both my uncle Louis and I knew we had to get Mama in the recording studio to capture her songs on tape. Working with just a guitarist and an autoharp player, Mama recorded her own versions of some of her favorite songs.

Dolly Parton, Carl Butler, Avie Lee Parton, Robert Lee Parton, and Pearl Butler.

In a recent development, the plan was to release an album, but for one reason or another, it never happened. Fortunately, my uncle Louis saved all the tapes, and when he passed away, his son Richie, who has always loved our family history and heritage, decided to clean them up and get them released.

Dolly Parton and her mother, Avie Lee Parton.

Recent findings suggest that many of them are well-known tunes, but you may know them under different titles. Like all mountain singers, Mama preferred to call songs by the name she’d learned them under, and we decided that that was the way we needed to present them to you.

If you’ve ever wondered where my music came from, this album tells the story, and I am so proud, happy, and honored to have shared this music and my mama’s voice with you.

Avie Lee Parton's Album, Mama Sings.

So Is The $100 GTA 6 Ultimate Edition Actually Worth It?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, before Grand Theft Auto 6 even debuted, there was some controversy online over the announcement of a $100 “Ultimate Edition” version of the game that would include access to a few exclusive shops and in-game cosmetics.
  • Sources indicate that in GTA 6, there are five stores that are locked behind the Ultimate Edition paywall.
  • Recent findings suggest that first up, there’s 305, a clothing store specializing in urban, skater-inspired clothing and gear.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, before Grand Theft Auto 6 even debuted, there was some controversy online over the announcement of a $100 “Ultimate Edition” version of the game that would include access to a few exclusive shops and in-game cosmetics. So, now that GTA 6 is here and I’ve spent over 150 hours with it, I can share what’s in the Ultimate Edition, how you access this stuff, and if it’s worth upgrading from the standard $80 version of GTA 6. The short version is…eh, probably not.

Sources indicate that in GTA 6, there are five stores that are locked behind the Ultimate Edition paywall. These stores include an exclusive tattoo parlor, street clothing shop, and hair salon. Now, at first, I thought it was pretty shitty of Rockstar to hide stores behind a paywall. And to be clear, it still does suck that a few shops are only accessible if you pay $20 more. But after playing GTA 6, I discovered that the world is filled with over 600 stores. There are already so many clothing, car, hair, make-up, and nail options in the base game. So the Ultimate Edition’s extra few stores don’t feel that necessary. And after actually visiting these shops and seeing what they have to offer, I don’t think people are missing out on that much.

Recent findings suggest that first up, there’s 305, a clothing store specializing in urban, skater-inspired clothing and gear. There’s some alright stuff in here, including some nice-looking jeans for Jason and a cool graphic shirt or two. And a really wild fuzzy hat for Lucia. But the options in here aren’t something you need to have. You can create plenty of great and cool outfits without stopping by this Ultimate Editionâonly retailer.

According to recent reports, next up is the tattoo shop Electric Fang. Of all the Ultimate Edition stores, this is the coolest one to enter. And I do think some of Electric Fang’s tat designs are solid. But again, there are so many other options in the game for ink that I’m not sure these are very necessary or worth the $20 upgrade.

Industry observers note that sara’s Unisex Salon might be the best of the bunch as it offers some stylish hairdos for both Jason and Lucia. But on top of that, it offers some really nice makeup options for Lucia and cool nail art, too. I ended up using some of these options during my time as Lucia because I liked them so much. Still, again, there are so many other good options for haircuts and nail art already in GTA 6 that I’m not sure you need to spend $20 more on this version.

It has been revealed that there are also two exclusive car mod garages in GTA 6‘s Ultimate Edition. One of them, Rideout Customs, offers some really gaudy and exotic paint and accessories options. If you wanted a neon-pink car with stripes painted to look like cheetah print, well, this is the place for you.

The other mod shop, One-Eyed Willie’s, is more useful. It offers up some really nice off-road options. There aren’t nearly as many off-road modding options in GTA 6 as there are for street cars, so losing out on access to this in the base game is a shame. I also love that One-Eyed Willie’s offers up a random paint job for every car in the game, including non-off-road vehicles, that you can only see once it’s applied. I brought my Banshee into the shop, and it received this pretty pink design that I loved.

Recent findings suggest that the Ultimate Edition also includes some unique free clothing items based on characters from an in-universe cartoon you can watch. These clothes are fine. I guess if you like the show a lot, they might be fun to wear. But…eh.

In a recent development, beyond the stores and cosmetics, there are some exclusive vehicles you get access to in the Ultimate Edition, but some of these are only available during chapter one for story reasons. The only thing from the Ultimate Edition I used regularly and still use often when I play is the Vapid off-road truck. It’s fast as heck, a great option for driving on the dirt, and can be upgraded into a beast that can hold a lot of stolen loot. There’s also a classic car scavenger hunt side mission hidden behind the paywall, but after 150 hours I’ve barely interacted with that thing.

In a recent development, answering the major question of “Is the Ultimate Edition worth it?” is tricky, because it depends entirely on what you value and your taste for fashion and cosmetics. I’ve provided some samples of what’s on offer and how it fits into the larger GTA 6 world.

My opinion is that if you can afford the extra $20, a few bits of the Ultimate Edition are nice and worth the upgrade. But for the most part, if you just want to play Grand Theft Auto 6 to enjoy the open world and its story, you don’t need this upgrade. You’ll have a great time with the base game and never think to yourself, “Boy, I wish there were 30 more shirts and a few more cars in this!” GTA 6 is already big. Don’t worry about making it a bit bigger.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Grand Theft Auto 6's launch day, more than half of everyone playing on PS5 and Xbox was playing GTA 6.

Citing new data from Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, analyst Mat Piscatella said on Bluesky that 61 percent of US PlayStation 5 players and 56 percent of global Xbox players who were active on 19th November "engaged with Grand Theft Auto 6".

PS5 players averaged 513 minutes in GTA 6 that day, which is over eight and a half hours, while Xbox players averaged 494 minutes, or around eight and a quarter hours.

"Both the DAU [daily active users] and minutes played engagement rates are absolutely bonkers," Piscatella wrote.

For comparison, Fortnite had the second-highest engagement rate that day, with 10 percent of active players across both platforms playing it.

Piscatella also shared the top five games that GTA 6 players had been playing in the two weeks before launch, between 6th and 19th November: Fortnite, Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto 5 (Remastered), Roblox, and NBA 2K27.

According to Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, Grand Theft Auto VI had a massive launch (surprise!).For players active on November 19th, 61% of US PlayStation 5 and 56% of global Xbox players engaged with Grand Theft Auto VI.PS5 GTA VI players averaged 513 minutes that day, Xbox players 494.

The figures come after Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 had become the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day.

GTA 6 debuted on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's one of the best-reviewed games of all time, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

In a recent development, eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

The Declasse Vamos is one of the many cars Moses asks you to steal for him in GTA 6, but like the BF Bandito, it's a little trickier than just grabbing it. When you reach the map marker, you'll realise the car is locked in a garage that requires a specific code to open it.

According to recent reports, the code to the door is 2727 and this is fixed. The way you discover this is by sneaking inside the trailer and looking at the number plate on the wall to the left of the window, just above the guy snoozing in the chair.

Enter the code to open the garage, break in with the slimjim, then hit the button to open the door. I personally incapacitated all of the people behind the trailer, so chances are they will pursue you or start shooting if you don't, once you try to drive out of there.

Now take the car back to Moses, being careful on the way, to earn $4,100ish for top condition.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

According to recent reports, I’ve played over 150 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6. You might think I’ve seen it all, and that I know everything there is to know about the game. Nope! I’m still discovering new mechanics, features, and open-world moments after all this time. This includes some very handy control shortcuts I recently learned about that will make your life in Vice City a little easier.

Industry observers note that first off, let’s start with the whole reason I wanted to write this blog. Did you know that you can promptly toggle your car radio on and off without having to enter a submenu? All you have to do is double-tap left on the D-pad, and Jason or Lucia will turn the radio on or off.

I had no idea you could do this until I saw people sharing it on Reddit. The game doesn’t explain this shortcut, as far as I can tell. I couldn’t even find it mentioned in the in-game help menu, which does include lots of other nifty tips and tricks.

Here’s another trick I just learned about: You can double-tap the circle/B button while in a car to cycle the headlights between off, high beams, and low beams.

I thought you had to hold left on the D-pad to open up the vehicle submenu to turn off the headlights, but nope! And again, this isn’t mentioned in the help menu and if a prompt appeared during the normal course of the game to explain this, I and many others must have missed it.

Here’s another useful thing you can do inside cars: If you double-tap the triangle/Y button while driving, you’ll exit the vehicle without turning off the engine or radio.

GTA 6‘s help menu does call this out and mentions you can do this at speed to have your car drive into something while you roll out the side to safely. But again, I can’t remember a single time when the game forced me to do this or taught me that it was possible. I learned from a random post online. I guess I should have dug through the help menu more, but come on, who is doing that in Grand Theft Auto?

Industry observers note that another feature mentioned in the help menu that I just learned about is the ability to click the right stick in and yell at nearby drivers. Rockstar refers to this as the road rage button, and it’s a good thing to have in a game where NPC drivers, inspired by real Floridian drivers, suck shit and drive like maniacs.

One more useful control trick: You can double-tap the triangle/Y button while driving a boat to get up and walk around the deck while the boat keeps on cruising.

In a recent development, the next time I boot up GTA 6, I’m going to start double-tapping random buttons during different parts of the game to see what other hidden shortcuts and control options Rockstar has buried in this massive game. And if you want some more useful hidden features, check out this blog about how to flip cars and sit anywhere you want in GTA 6.Â.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nicalis has removed AI-generated music from The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ after players discovered it in the game's latest enhancement, prompting a wave of negative reviews on Steam.

Industry observers note that the music in question was tied to a run themed around Grand Theft Auto 6, which launched on the same day (19th November). A day later, Reddit user ShweetsStuff posted that the run's music was "100% generated by Suno (AI) (with proof)", pointing to tracks that reference the AI music tool Suno in their metadata.

"Thanks, Nicalis, for breaking everything and adding AI slop to an already-existing game!" one Steam review reads (thanks, IGN).

"I'm starting to think that adding AI to a game should be valid grounds [for] refunds to people who have already paid for and played a game," stated another.

Woke up to a shit show, obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.

Responding to the criticism, Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen said he "woke up to a shit show".

It has been revealed that "Obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned," he wrote on X/Twitter, before inviting players to report issues and bugs to the email address shared in one of Nicalis' tweets, which confirmed it had "pushed a new build with critical fixes", including the "removal of generated music files". The patch is live on PC, and Nicalis indicates it has been submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo, and Sony.

Nicalis has yet to explain how the music ended up in the game.

Hi All!Repentance+ Revision:The team has pushed a latest build with critical fixes.• Removal of generated music files• Larynx + Car Battery Bug Fix• PC patch—should be live already• Submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo and Sony ASAPAdditional: • Continuing work on netcode… pic.twitter.com/d1gyLUlBK8.

Industry observers note that following the gigantic Afterbirth and Afterbirth+ expansions, released in 2015 and 2017 respectively, The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth grew again with 2021's community-inspired, sequel-sized Repentance DLC. That was meant to be the last content drop for real, yet 2024 gave us the free Repentance+ DLC, which finally added online co-op to the disturbingly charming roguelike. The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth has since hit a latest concurrent player record on Steam 12 years after it was released.

McMillen's most recent game, Mewgenics, also made quite a splash earlier this year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you've noticed that Grand Theft Auto 6's Jason Duval isn't much of a talker, that's by design, as his quiet nature was inspired by Steve McQueen and the studio's research into former Army Rangers.

Speaking to Destructoid over email, Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained that the team looked at classic couple-on-the-run films when it decided on GTA 6's story.

"When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was Peckinpah's The Getaway," Humphries said. "Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite.".

Sources indicate that that approach also fitted the studio's research into veterans. "This also resonated with the research we were doing around veterans and particularly former Army Rangers (in our world we call them Marauders)," Humphries continued. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves.".

Game writer Michael Wiafe mentioned Florida's real-life crime stories were "an obvious starting point" for GTA 6's characters more broadly.

"From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe noted. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn't necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don't attempt to make excuses for them.".

Fellow writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern added that while "the story takes some pretty heavy turns", Jason and Lucia's goal remains consistent. "So sharing their sense of determination, the focus on their goal, through all the highs and lows - that's what I hope people feel more than anything. You really want them to make it.".

GTA 6 released on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, not everyone is happy: some players have been review bombing its Metacritic user score over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I'd just stolen my very first airplane in GTA 6 and was happily cruising over the city when I looked out my window and saw an enormous purple building. I banked, slowed down, and flew a bit closer to read the huge sign on the roof.

Recent findings suggest that oh, hell yes. I was so excited to throw my carefully accumulated three hundred dollars away on poker and slots that I immediately attempted my very first landing. After the explosion and my miraculous resurrection, I rushed back to the casino and crashed again, this time with my body into the locked front doors.

The casino in GTA 6 is closed. Trust me, I tried every door, and the only one that opened was a utility closet.

I was early into my playthrough, still in Chapter 1 of the GTA 6 story missions, so I thought maybe there'll be some mission that unlocks the casino so I can play some poker, try my luck at the slots, and maybe bet on the also-closed dog track—I assume it's a dog track because I've seen dogs in GTA 6, but no horses—that's right next door to the casino.

It has been revealed that nope! I'm now 100% done with the main story and that casino is still closed. And that's not the only business in GTA 6 that isn't open for business. Not even a half-mile away from the casino there's a go-cart track called Hot Skidz sporting a huge "Coming Soon" sign. I saw that early in my game as well, and checked back later. Still closed. I also found a second, smaller casino. Also closed.

What a letdown. I managed to get my motorcycle onto the go-cart track, and as I drove glumly around it, alone, having no fun, I perked up a bit. Maybe this just gives me something to look forward to. A hint of more singleplayer content that'll be coming to GTA 6 next year. Hopefully next year.

There's already a lot of seemingly unfinished stuff in GTA 6, partial systems that could be added to and completed, like:.

Industry observers note that I felt better after that, but as I went back to stare at that huge, closed casino—which is all lit up at night like it's actually open, even though it is not open, and I know this because I rechecked all the doors—I remembered how the casino in GTA 5 worked. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You Must Remember This is a podcast dedicated, as its host Karina Longworth notes in every intro, to exploring the secret and/or forgotten histories of Hollywood’s first century. Longworth, who is an LA–based writer and film preservationist, usually tells her stories in themed seasons. Those include Erotic 90’s, spanning the introduction of the NC-17 rating to Eyes Wide Shut; Dead Blondes (Marilyn Monroe, Jean Harlow, Veronica Lake); and a whole series exploring the web of connections Charles Manson had to Hollywood. It’s addictive, exhaustively researched, and narrated in a way that is both soothing and trancelike.

Longworth is a native Angeleno who has been writing about film for years. She was a film editor and critic at the LA Weekly for three years until 2012; wrote books on Al Pacino and Meryl Streep; and then started You Must Remember This is 2014. She’s also part of a film-loving couple: her husband of 8 years is the Knives Out writer and director Rian Johnson.

The latest season of the podcast is called The Bisexuals, spotlighting the stories of actors and actresses whose love lives were often much more diverse than anything sanctioned by a studio. One star that the season discusses is Libby Holman, a singer and socialite who married the tobacco heir Zachary Smith Reynolds in 1931. Not only did she have a fruitful sex life with Tallulah Bankhead and Montgomery Clift, but she was known for her signature scent called Jungle Gardenia.

In honor of that bombastic perfume that wafted off of her, Longworth, 46, collaborated with Joey Rosin, who formulated a fragrance, Bisexual. Vanity Fair spoke to Longworth about moviegoing in Los Angeles versus Fresh York, what she smelled like as a teenager, being in grad school in your 40s, and her thoughts about Quentin Tarantino’s film programming.

The interview that follows has been condensed for length and clarity.

Vanity Fair: What was the first perfume you remember wearing?

Karina Longworth: Opium by YSL was really a significant deal for me when I was 18, 19. It was one of the first perfumes that I ever knew about. I started with The Body Shop’s Tea Rose oil. I didn’t really have any female adult influences because my mom died when I was 11, and so I had to sort of figure out that whole world.

Have you always wanted to make a perfume? Are you a perfume nerd?

So I never had an ambition to make a perfume, but over the past 10 years, I’ve become really into perfume. I used to rent an office space in the same building as an independent perfumer, Jacqueline Ella Steele, whose brand was called Goest— which doesn’t exist anymore—but she made a perfume called Silent Films. She was the first person I contacted about trying to formulate this perfume. But she’s out of business. So that’s when I started asking around and I got led to Joey Rosin.

The idea came from your research?

In a recent development, I got the idea because, in reading and writing about Libby Holman, there are all these anecdotes of her walking into a room in a cloud of Jungle Gardenia, to the point where, people who were attracted to her were attracted to it, and people who didn’t like her found it so disgusting. I thought there was something really interesting about that, how the same scent could be either attractive or repellent, depending on how you felt about the person wearing it.

What does a bisexual smell like? In this case jungles and gardenia.

Personalities, voices and clothes all depend on who’s doing it.

Sources indicate that there’s this really incredible anecdote in Patricia Bosworth’s Montgomery Clift biography about how one of Montgomery Clift’s friends was at a party at Treetops, Libby Holman’s estate, and she was looking for the bathroom, and accidentally walked into her bedroom, and the bed was a tangle of white satin sheets, and there’s a giant bottle of barbiturates on the nightstand and everything just reeked of Jungle Gardenia. She was grossed out, but then she also got the impression this is Libby and Monty’s sex lair.

Were you trying to recreate the smell?

We didn’t try to copy the exact old fragrance. Joey does his research, and he did research into what the original notes were. But we talked about not wanting it to be a slavish copy, and instead just trying to evoke for both of us what jungle would smell like with gardenia, and how that could evoke Libby’s story. And so we played around with adding different types of smoke to it.

Have you ever been in a jungle?

Industry observers note that I’ve been to Tahiti. I’m trying to think if I’ve ever been to a jungle. We talked a lot about tropical plants and what the dirt would smell like, and the heat. It’s like hot weather almost has a smell. But then pairing that with this kind of old lady scent of gardenia. I went to visit his studio in Brooklyn a few times and he mailed some samples to me in Los Angeles. And by that point, it was like four iterations that were almost exactly the same. So it was just about what was giving me the best vibe.

You were living in LA for the process?

I was living alone in Rochester, N.Y. in a depressing situation because of the weather and being very alone, having no social life.

According to recent reports, but you loved your grad school program, right? I forget the name but I know it’s long.

Industry observers note that L. Jeffrey Selznick School of Film Preservation at the George Eastman Museum. I got so much out of the program, but it was grueling, physically, and mentally, and emotionally. It was really difficult to suddenly be living alone in a place where I felt like I had no one I could really talk to.

So you were in an entirely new, but temporary situation.

Industry observers note that I started relying on scented candles to improve my mood and to change my mood. If I got home feeling terrible, the fragrance was helpful. I also had nowhere to wear perfume. At first I thought I would just make a candle, and then as I started learning more about fragrance, I learned that candles have to go through a much more rigorous process. And it takes a lot longer. We were not going to be able to get it done in time to have a presale like we have during the podcast season. But in the future, I would like to do a signature scent for You Must Remember This and have it available as a perfume and a candle.

It would be classic, but in a different way. I’m very inspired by the signature scent that they have at the Chateau [Marmont].

There has been a lot of talk about moviegoing being back. How has your tour been?

Sources indicate that it has been great. In Savannah they sold 400 tickets to a very obscure, pre-code movie on a Friday night.

People must ask you a lot of podcast questions. What are your tips?

I say I don’t know what form yours is going to take, but mine takes the form of writing an extremely detailed script, and then sitting by myself in a room and reading it into a microphone.

I built a recording studio. I bought a little house in Laurel Canyon at the end of a private road, like at the end of a cul-de-sac, but you feel like you’re in the middle of the forest. I bought it from this woman who had lived there for 15 years and was kind of an all-purpose healer. She basically built a soundproof room with clay on the walls and crystals embedded into the clay, where she would do sound baths with them. When I saw this house, it was just perfect.

Which city has a better movie scene, Fresh York or LA?

Fresh York’s way better than LA, but LA is getting better.

Recent findings suggest that did someone buy the Vista? I loved that theater.

[Quentin] Tarantino owns the Vista. Because it’s Tarantino, he won’t let them show anything digital. It has to be a film print, and so he’ll show a new movie if there’s a print, like The Odyssey played there, Sinners played there. But when there isn’t a new movie out that is on a print, he programs whatever he wants to see. He also does a lot of like Saturday morning matinees of classical Hollywood cinema that is just his taste, you know. Sometimes it’s my taste, sometimes it’s not. It’s a lot of Jerry Lewis. But one thing I will say for Tarantino is that when he discovers a filmmaker or genre or something from the past, he shows. He’s been showing all these William Beaudine silent films, and I think that’s great because silent film has really fallen out of fashion in LA.

I was leaving to interview you today and someone noted, “Oh, I love that podcast,” and was talking about the Manson series. Is that your most popular?

It changes. Increasingly, people are asking about the Polly Platt series.

Do you know what the next series is going to be?

I have two ideas that would involve talking to people or family members of subjects who have passed away, but who could give me access to sort of the family lore. I am in contact with both of those families, but I need to kind of do the legwork, talking to them more and figure out which story makes the most sense. I also sketched out a very long season about the three stars of Rebel Without a Cause. That is something that people have been asking me to do for years. But the thing that stops me from doing it is that we still don’t know exactly what happened to Natalie Wood. But that’s kind of in my back pocket.

Red Dead is in a similar lane to The Last of Us, which HBO managed to thread the needle on making into a prestige television show that still hooked fans of the game. It’s easy to imagine a similarly placed streamer doing the same for Rockstar’s IP, with internal executives pointing to mood boards that include the critical success of things like Deadwood and the commercial appeal of things like Yellowstone.

So we donât rule it out, but weâre very, very selective.â.

He’d given shareholders a more detailed account of this reasoning back in 2023 during Hollywood’s Barbenheimer-craze”.

The hit ratios in the motion picture business are vastly lower than they are in the interactive entertainment business. Our hit ratios for console properties are in the 80 percent or 90 percent. The hit ratio for a well-run movie studio is around 30 percent, which is to say there’s a 70 percent chance that the movie that we license could fail. And so in success, the number, in terms of the benefit to our bottom line…it’s not zero, but it’s not really material to what we do around here. And in failure, we run the risk of compromising the underlying intellectual property.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let people scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers. But the company discontinued the service at the start of 2026, with upcoming scans stopping on Jan. 15 and all accounts deleted on Feb. 16.

In a recent development, google indicates it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for users whose data was found on the dark web. Google promised a new service that would provide more actionable intel, but that service has yet to materialize, and there haven’t been any further announcements about it yet.

Dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let users run scans free of cost. Now that it’s gone, however, there are plenty of other services that offer the same service at varying costs and levels of effectiveness. Let’s talk through the nature of the insight that Google's reports offered, how it collected that information in the first place, and what options exist in the market to replace it.

Google introduced the Dark Web Report in March 2023 as a premium feature available to Google One users, but later extended it for free to anyone with a Google account and moved it to the "Results about you" dashboard.

You'd set up a monitoring profile with your name, date of birth, physical address, phone number, emails, and Social Security Number if you lived in the U.S. After that, you could head to the dashboard anytime you wanted to run a free scan across dark web forums and marketplaces, publicly disclosed corporate data breaches, and other hidden online spaces to see if any of your personal information had shown up there. It was easy to use—but not a lot of people knew it existed in the first place.

It’s unclear what prompted the internal decision at Google, but in the absence of concrete next steps, it is reasonable to think the reports could create panic for the uninitiated. There’s no way to remove your information from the dark web once it’s already in circulation there. Still, having an early warning so you could reset 2FA or self-lock your SSN isn’t without merit.

But perhaps more importantly, most people with Google accounts didn’t know and hadn’t heard of the Dark Web Report’s existence. Google has likely taken it as a hint that customers want more active remediation tools than simple alerts, which is why it’s now directing users to the Password Manager, Passkeys, and “Results about you” dashboard instead—though, again, the firm hasn't followed through on a direct replacement for Dark Web Report, despite teasing such a feature.

Many of the top dark web scanners draw from the same well of information, scanning against major data breaches and dark web spaces. Several also offer breach notifications that send you email alerts when your details show up in a periodic scan. However, none of that is worth paying for because Have I Been Pwned or Mozilla Monitor cover those features quite well for free. Even the default password managers from Google and Apple come with some ability to monitor leaked credentials.

According to recent reports, there isn’t an easy way to scrub your information from the dark web once it ends up getting leaked. But you can take steps to protect sensitive information or financial data once you know there’s been a leak. If a password has been compromised, reset it immediately. Also, enable 2FA on the affected account for added security. Even better, switch to a passkey if that account supports it. If not, authenticator apps are a safer way to receive 2FA codes than standard SMS.

In a recent development, if your Social Security number has been leaked, freeze your credit with Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. You can do this by contacting each agency separately. Freezing your credit will prevent unauthorized credit withdrawals and protect your credit score from abuse by attackers. If one of your credit or debit card numbers has ended up in a breach, call your bank to freeze transactions on that card immediately.

Finally, get in the habit of using email aliases instead of sharing your actual email address with every platform and service provider. Addy.io and Proton’s SimpleLogin are both popular services that let you generate temporary email aliases that point to your inbox.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In GTA 6, you can find many radio stations playing hundreds of songs.
